title: Full Fury vs Joshua undercard confirmed with unusual running order
summary: Welsh star Joe Cordina and Tyson Fury’s brother Roman will both feature
content: The full undercard for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua has been confirmed, with an unusual running order in place . The standout addition on Wednesday was Welsh star and former world champion Joe Cordina , who faces Mauricio Lara in an intriguing lightweight bout. However, the fight will headline the preliminary card at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, rather than taking place on the main card. That move alone has led to further criticism of the main card, which was already seen as underwhelming by many fans . Joe Cordina (left) during a win in July 2025 (Getty) Also on the prelims will be Fury’s brother Roman, taking on Adam Kolarik at heavyweight, while British super-welterweight prospect Odel Kamara steps out for just the second time, fighting Patrik Matejcek. Two of the other bouts feature Japanese brothers Hayato Tsutsumi and Reito Tsutsumi, who respectively face Vic Pasillas at featherweight and Muheeb Fazeldin at super-featherweight. Mikie Tallon will feature in an all-British super-flyweight tilt with Sean Bruce, Saudi prospect Mohammed Alakel boxes Rogger Rivera at super-featherweight, and Constantino Nanga fights Lerrone Richards at light-heavyweight. These contests support the main card, which will be headlined by the heavyweight clash between Fury and Joshua – arguably the biggest British fight in history. In fact, the main card consists solely of heavyweight fights, with the chief-support bout pitting Deontay Wilder against Martin Bakole. The latter was originally paired with Solomon Adebayo, who was pulled from the event as Bakole stepped up to replace the injured Jai Opetaia against Wilder. Deontay Wilder (left) is a three-time opponent of Tyson Fury, losing to the Briton twice and drawing once (Getty) Rounding out the main card, Moses Jolly boxes Igor Adiel Macedo and Da’Mazion Vanhouter fights Michael Essomba. The event will take place on Friday 11 December, streaming live exclusively on Netflix. Wednesday brought the news that main-event ring walks will begin at 1am GMT on Saturday 12 December, with travel plans and police presence also confirmed .

title: ESPN’s Desmond Howard Makes His Stance Clear on Alabama’s Controversial Ranking
summary: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During…
content: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; ESPN personality Desmond Howard arrives at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During Wednesday’s edition of ESPN’s “Get Up,” Howard discussed the committee’s decision to move Alabama from No. 3 to No. 6. The Crimson Tide fell behind Texas, Notre Dame and Tennessee despite improving to 9-2 with Saturday’s victory over Chattanooga. However, Howard believes the committee made the correct decision. “I thought they finally got it right,” Howard said. The ESPN analyst questioned why Alabama had remained ahead of teams with stronger victories in previous rankings. In particular, Howard pointed toward Texas and its collection of quality wins. The Longhorns moved to No. 3 after spending recent weeks behind Alabama. Howard Points to a Major Difference Between Alabama and Texas Howard believes the committee should prioritize the quality of each team’s victories when evaluating playoff contenders. Texas has defeated Ohio State, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU this season. Meanwhile, Alabama does not currently own a victory over a team ranked in the committee’s latest top 25. That difference played a significant role in Howard’s assessment. The analyst also questioned why Texas had remained behind Alabama despite its stronger collection of ranked victories. For Howard, the results on the field should carry more weight than a team’s reputation. His comments add another prominent ESPN voice to the debate surrounding Alabama’s playoff résumé. Tennessee Also Moves Ahead of Alabama Texas wasn’t the only SEC program to pass Alabama in Tuesday’s rankings. Tennessee climbed to No. 5, moving one position ahead of the Crimson Tide. The Volunteers defeated Alabama 26-10 earlier this season, giving Tennessee a valuable head-to-head advantage. However, Alabama had remained ahead of Tennessee in previous committee rankings. That changed Tuesday after the Volunteers improved their record with a victory over LSU. College Football Playoff selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek explained that the committee had reevaluated the teams’ résumés. The latest rankings now place Texas third, Tennessee fifth and Alabama sixth. All three programs enter rivalry weekend with identical 9-2 records. Alabama Faces Important Iron Bowl Test Howard’s comments arrive just days before Alabama hosts Auburn in the annual Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide will welcome the Tigers to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28. Alabama enters the matchup with an opportunity to strengthen its playoff position and preserve its conference championship hopes. Meanwhile, Auburn will attempt to disrupt those ambitions. title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
summary: Exeter City manager Matt Taylor says his side is "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form.
content: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. This isn't an easy place to come to but we've got to make sure our energy is in the right place on Saturday." All the latest Exeter City news

title: Georgia vs Georgia Tech scouting report, bold predictions, injury updates
summary: Georgia football and Georgia Tech meet in a Week 13 game. Here are four bold predictions, players we are watching and a pick.
content: Just a year ago, “Clean, Ole Fashioned Hate” between Georgia football and Georgia Tech was a top 25 matchup. Now the in-state rivals meet Saturday in Athens with the Bulldogs ranked No. 1 in the nation and the Yellow Jackets a 3-8 team that is tied for last in the 17-team ACC. “I know they haven't had the kind of season that they want to have, but I also know that records can be thrown out the window when it comes to this game,” Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. “The physicality in this game's unmatched. I think that's what you look for in a rivalry game.” Georgia has won its last four games this season: 27-8, 42-7, 48-21 and 34-6. The Yellow Jackets have lost five of their last six including, 50-29, at home to Wake Forest last Saturday. Georgia is a 35 ½ point favorite. “Someone showed me the ESPN predictor or whatever,” Georgia Tech coach Brent Key said. “I said, ‘Awesome, so you’re telling me we’ve got a chance.'” A beat-up Georgia Tech team will be without injured quarterback Grady Adamson who has helped boost the running game. Starter Alberto Mendoza’s status for the game is up in the air after leaving last week’s game injured. Georgia-Georgia Tech still brings out some bad feelings between the teams even with more roster movement in the transfer portal era. “It’s hate week,” Georgia defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye said. “We don’t really like these dudes. The aura around the building is kind of different when we play these guys.” Georgia vs. Georgia Tech predictions Even if all of its quarterbacks were available, Georgia Tech would face a major challenge against a Bulldogs defense that is sixth in the nation in yards (267.0) and points allowed (13.9) per game. Georgia Tech is 95 th in the nation in scoring at 24.0 points per game. The Yellow Jackets have been using two quarterbacks, but Adamson is out reportedly with a collarbone injury. He rushed 143 yards on 16 carries and a touchdown last week against Wake Forest and 96 yards on 19 carries and a touchdown against Clemson two weeks ago. If Mendoza (54 th in the nation in pass efficiency, 11 TD passes, 7 INT) can’t go, third-string quarterback Graham Knowles will get the call. He rushed for a 7-yard touchdown late in last week’s game. “It’s got to be the next man up right now,” Key said Wednesday on 680 AM in Atlanta. “We’ll see where the other guys are from a health standpoint as we get closer to the game. Graham will have to get out there. Fortunately he was able to get some reps at the end of the game last week. ...We’ll put a package together that he’s able to go execute.” Georgia vs. Georgia Tech scouting report Why Georgia has an advantage: The Bulldogs are playing their best football of the season since the open date following the loss to Auburn. Despite being a huge favorite, setting a record for longest winning streak in series history against the rival Yellow Jackets should be motivation enough on what will be Senior Day. Why Georgia Tech has an advantage: The Yellow Jackets can lean on that they have managed to stay within striking distance of Georgia the last few games including the 8OT Bulldog win in 2024. There will be no bowl game for Georgia Tech which can make its season with a shocker by shortening the game with time-consuming possessions and forcing several turnovers. Georgia vs. Georgia Tech injury updates Georgia: C Drew Bobo (back, questionable), WR Landon Roldan (ankle, questionable), OLB Amaris Williams (knee, out). Georgia Tech: QB Grady Adamson (collarbone, out), QB Fernando Mendoza (undisclosed, gametime decision), RB Malachi Holsey (undisclosed, out) , CB Jaylan Mbawke (undisclosed, out), CB Kelvin Hill (unidisclosed, out), DE Jordan Boyd (undisclosed, out), RB Chad Alexander (undisclosed, out), S Savion Riley (undisclosed, out), WR Darnell Collins (undisclosed, out), CB Trae Stevenson (undisclosed, out), S Fenix Felton (undisclosed, out), S Will Kiker (undisclosed, out), LB Kyle Efford (shoulder, out), OL Kevin Peay (undisclosed, out), OL Markell Samuel (undisclosed, out), OL Ethan Mackenny (undisclosed, out), WR Kentrell Davis (undisclosed, out), TE Kevin Roche (undisclosed, out), DE AJ Hoffler (undisclosed, out). Prediction Georgia 49, Georgia Tech 7: Georgia is playing with all kinds of confidence. Georgia Tech's season can't end soon enough. The Yellow Jackets rank 134th in the FBS in stopping the run, worst among P4 teams. That should make for a long day against a Georgia offensive line that rushed for more than 200 yards in four SEC games. Georgia vs. Georgia Tech scouting report: What we're watching Georgia defense: Will this be a typical Georgia defensive showing from a unit that has held three of its last four opponents to 8 or fewer points or has there been any distraction from defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann accepting the Florida State job on Monday and presumably working to assemble a staff. Justice Haynes: The son of former Georgia running back Verron Haynes is at his third college stop after Alabama and Michigan. He's rushed for 806 yards and 6 touchdowns this season including 116 yards on 13 carries in a win at Clemson two weeks ago. Can Chauncey Bowens get going?: The Georgia junior running back has 3 carries for 9 yards and a touchdown in two games back from a lower leg injury. Getting him back closer to pre-injury form could keep Nate Frazier fresh for the postseason after he rushed for 94 yards on 23 carries last week. Georgia Tech linebacker EJ Lightsey: The 6-foot-2, 230-pound fifth-year senior has started 26 games over the last three seasons for the Yellow Jackets. He had a career-high 12 tackles last year against Georgia where he spent his first two seasons in 2022 and 2023. He's fifth on the team with 47 tackles this year. Bold predictions for Georgia football vs Georgia Tech Gunner Stockton builds some Heisman momentum: Gunner Stockton isn't quite in the territory for an invite to New York for the Heisman Trophy but the quarterback of the No. 1 team in the country will build some more momentum with his showing in this game. The Yellow Jackets are 125th in the nation in total defense. Lawson Luckie time: On Senior Day, the Georgia tight end gets multiple catches for the first time since the Auburn game. Georgia's tight ends should be able to create mismatches against Georgia Tech's linebackers. Luckie has 15 catches for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns this season. Yellow Jackets dig into bag of tricks: Brent Key was asked this week how he can get his team to play confident but not tight. "First off, what do we have to lose? There's no reason to be uptight. None at all. Throw caution to the wind." Look for that to translate into a trick play or two and even a fake on special teams. Georgia slows down Tech ground game: Georgia Tech has rushed for 269 yards and 289 yards the last two games, but running QB Grady Adamson's absence will be felt and the Bulldogs will hold Justice Haynes and Trelain Maddox in check. title: Iowa announces Nebraska game is sold out
summary: The Iowa athletic department has announced that the Black Friday game against Nebraska is sold out.
content: The Iowa Athletics Department has announced that Friday's Pioneer Heroes Game against Nebraska at Kinnick Stadium is sold out . The game kicks off at 11 a.m. CT and will be televised on CBS. Iowa (9-2, 6-2) has sold out 35 consecutive games at Kinnick Stadium, dating back to the start of the 2022 season. Nebraska (7-4, 4-4) has a home sellout streak that currently stands at 417 consecutive games. Nebraska is coming off a 31-28 victory over Ohio State last Saturday in Lincoln. The victory was the Huskers' first over a ranked opponent since 2016 (35-31 win against No. 22 Oregon ). Iowa enters Friday's game following a 34-17 win at Illinois last weekend. The Hawkeyes are on a four-game winning streak and are still in the running for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. The Hawkeyes were ranked 15th in last week's College Football Playoff rankings and are still in the running for a spot in the final Big Ten Championship Game. Iowa has appeared in the title game three times (2015, 2021, 2023) and is 0-3 as a program. Friday's game is the 57th all-time meeting between these two schools and the 16th meeting as Big Ten Conference opponents. Nebraska leads the series 30-23-3 all-time but Iowa has an 11-4 series lead as Big Ten opponents. title: Lane Kiffin Forced to Address Controversial On-Air Moment as LSU Frustrations Boil Over
summary: BATON ROUGE, La. — LSU football coach Lane Kiffin is no stranger to controversy, but his latest public remarks created an uncomfortable moment for the Tigers’ own broadcasting crew. Kiffin addressed the incident during his weekly news conference Monday, apologizing for an emotional outburst that aired on the LSU Sports Radio Network during Saturday’s 27-13 loss to Tennessee. The apology followed the circulation of a…
content: Nov 21, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Louisiana State head coach Lane Kiffin reacts after a play against the Tennessee Volunteers during the second half at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — LSU football coach Lane Kiffin is no stranger to controversy, but his latest public remarks created an uncomfortable moment for the Tigers’ own broadcasting crew. Kiffin addressed the incident during his weekly news conference Monday, apologizing for an emotional outburst that aired on the LSU Sports Radio Network during Saturday’s 27-13 loss to Tennessee. The apology followed the circulation of a video showing the reaction of LSU’s radio announcers, who appeared caught off guard by the coach’s language. Kiffin’s Remarks Leave LSU Radio Booth Stunned The incident occurred during Kiffin’s halftime interview with LSU sideline reporter Gordy Rush at Neyland Stadium. LSU trailed Tennessee 10-6 after a controversial targeting penalty against Tigers safety Ty Benefield helped the Volunteers score a touchdown shortly before halftime. Kiffin initially discussed LSU’s offensive struggles before using two profanities to criticize the targeting decision. The remarks immediately created an awkward situation for LSU’s broadcast team. Video from the radio booth showed play-by-play announcer Chris Blair removing his headset and putting his head in his hands. Analyst Jacob Hester subsequently handled the transition to a commercial break. The clip circulated on social media, drawing attention to the unusual exchange during an otherwise routine halftime interview. LSU Coach Issues Public Apology Kiffin opened his Monday news conference by addressing the incident. “I want to apologize for my language at halftime in the interview,” Kiffin said. “No excuses.” He acknowledged his frustration with the first half and said he had difficulty hearing the question because of the noise inside Neyland Stadium. However, the coach made clear that neither circumstance justified his language. “But there’s no reason for that,” Kiffin said. “And so, to people who were offended, I apologize for that.” Although Kiffin apologized for his wording, he maintained his disagreement with the targeting penalty. Benefield was ejected following a tackle on Tennessee tight end DaSaahn Brame late in the second quarter. The penalty helped extend Tennessee’s possession, which ended with Brame catching the go-ahead touchdown. Kiffin subsequently questioned the application of the targeting rule while discussing the play with reporters. Frustrations Mount During Difficult LSU Season The controversy comes during a disappointing stretch for LSU in Kiffin’s first season leading the program. The Tigers have lost three consecutive games, falling to Alabama, Texas and Tennessee during November. LSU enters its regular-season finale against Arkansas with a 6-5 record, including a 3-5 mark in Southeastern Conference play. Kiffin has repeatedly emphasized his confidence in the program’s future while acknowledging the team’s difficulty finishing close games. During his Sunday conference call, the coach also indicated that LSU would evaluate multiple aspects of the program after the season. “We’ll look at everything,” Kiffin said, referencing positions, schemes and coaches. For now, LSU’s attention turns toward Saturday’s matchup with Arkansas in Fayetteville. However, Kiffin’s latest viral moment has provided another reminder of the scrutiny surrounding his turbulent debut season in Baton Rouge. title: Tide starters listed on Availability Report for Iron Bowl vs. Auburn
summary: Alabama received some good news on Wednesday night's initial Availability Report, while Auburn has a very important player whose status is unknown.
content: The initial SEC Availability Report for Saturday's Iron Bowl between Alabama and Auburn has been released, and for the Crimson Tide in particular, it appears a number of key players are trending in the right direction. Released on Wednesday night, Alabama had 11 total players listed on the initial report, seven of which will miss the Iron Bowl. Each of those seven listed were expected going into Wednesday night, meaning there were no surprises in terms of players listed as "out." However, there were in fact some surprises when it came to the others listed, as Alabama has four players officially carrying a "probable" tag ahead of the Iron Bowl. Among those were starting inside linebackers Luke Metz and Caleb Woodson, as well as rotational defensive lineman Fatutoa Henry. The biggest surprise though is outside linebacker Desmond Umeozulu, who was also listed as probable, and as a result, appears to be nearing a potential return in Week 13. Umeozulu, a senior transfer from South Carolina, has missed a majority of the season due to injury, and has not played since the Florida State game. For Auburn, undoubtedly the biggest takeaway from Wednesday night's report was starting quarterback Byrum Brown, who is listed as "questionable." Should Brown potentially miss the Iron Bowl, then backup Tristan Ti'a would likely get the start. Following is a look at Wednesday night's initial Week 13 Availability Report for the Iron Bowl showdown between Alabama and Auburn. title: Everton Under 21s fall short as another cruel deflection goes against them
summary: A narrow victory for Tranmere but Matos shows mettle
content: Melvin Matos and a few others shone against League Two opponents | Getty Images On a cold but dry November Tuesday night, Dave Hughes’ young Everton Under 21 side made the 6 mile trip under the River Mersey and through Birkenhead to take on League Two opponents and their second-nearest neighbours, Tranmere Rovers. The contest was part of the appetisingly-named Jersey Mike’s Subs trophy, otherwise known as the Football League Trophy. Everton sat bottom of the 4 team group going into the game so pride was the main prize. The side named by Hughes featured 16 year old Jonathan Nsangou up as the lone striker, ably supported by the attacking midfield trio of Omari Benjamin, Malik Olayiwola and Braiden Graham. That came as a bit of a surprise to all concerned as the easy assumption was that the more experienced 20 year old Benjamin would lead the line. We didn’t get the chance to see any of David Moyes’ fringe players getting a chance or former Blue and non-contract player Tom Davies either. Shame as the extra experience would have made a difference on the night, not to mention giving a few players some actual competitive minutes!!!! The side was as below: View Link In an entertaining and well-contested match, the young Blues certainly held their own in the opening exchanges with the defence looking more solid than I have seen them this season. The midfield duo of Harvey Foster and Melvin Matos ahead of them also had a good blend of control under pressure and a bit of bite. First real chance fell the Blues’ way after 19 minutes. 18 year old John Dodds, looking the part alongside the powerful captain Will Tamen, intercepted near the half way line and played the ball forward to Olayiwola who saw Graham point where he wanted it. He delivered it perfectly and the young Northern Irishman did what he does best, score in a one v one with the ‘keeper. 1-0 and looking good! Six minutes later and those two players combined again as a neat flick by Olayiwola at the edge of the penalty area allowed Graham to cut inside and he saw his goal-bound drive deflected for a corner. The next chance came as Olayiwola was crowded out near the centre circle by two Rovers players and a smart pass through to Kamara. He got behind Tamen and beat ‘keeper Fraser Barnsley and the despairing tackle from young Dodds. To be honest, at first sight I thought the player was definitely offside but there were few Toffes protests and, of course, no VAR, 1-1. See their goal below. 🔥 A well-taken first Rovers goal from David Kamara. Match highlights: https://t.co/5slsk6nLnB #TRFC #SWA pic.twitter.com/BnuQzAfZIU — Tranmere Rovers FC (@TranmereRovers) November 25, 2026 Immediately before half-time , Matos, hemmed in near the left touchline, swivelled and got himself free and lashed a left-footed volley across goal from an acute angle, glancing the crossbar and causing panic for the home goalkeeper. This (below) is a still of the action immediately before the audacious shot. View Link Shortly after the second half started, Dodds went down for the 2nd time in the match and had to give way, hopefully as a precaution, with Luis Gardner replacing him alongside Tamen. Almost immediately, the irrepressible Matos tumbled in the penalty area under a challenge and it looked a fair shout but wasn’t given. As Toffees’ current luck would have it, just 3 minutes after we could have been ahead again, we were behind and, you guessed it, a 16-yard shot by Veevers was deflected over Barnsley by Tamen who had thrown his body in the way of the shot, 1-2. As the game flowed end to end, Barnsley made a smart near post save then Olayiwola set up Matos on the edge of the area and his shot left the crossbar shaking for several seconds afterwards. After 77 minutes, familiar face, former Blue and lifelong Evertonian Lewis Warrington came on against his old team-mates to try to shore things up. Everton pressed with Shea Pita feeding fellow sub George Finney for a goal-bound shot and yet again, Matos who volleyed straight at the goalkeeper in the 90+1 minute. So it ended in a 1-2 defeat but the Blues gave a really good account of themselves, so who stood out? It won’t surprise you to hear me say Melvin Matos who was excellent on the night, a cross between N’Golo Kante and Gana Gueye. There’s a fearlessness about him, he has strength, tackles anything and everything, has pace, a bit of trickery and an eye for a shot. His energy alone should have him fast-tracked for senior development in my humble opinion. Besides Matos, Malik Olayiwola was really good with his energy and trickery, Harvey Foster with his elegant movement and passing range, Dodds and Tamen were solid and left-back Josh Van Schoor was back to his very best. Nsangou had a quiet game, did nothing wrong but there were only glimpses of his undoubted talent. Maybe centre-forward for him is too tough an ask at this stage, he needed to be on the ball more, not competing in the air with six-foot defenders. Graham took his goal well and a few other good pieces but again one of his quieter games. Next up for the Under 21s is a home Premier League 2 game with Leeds United on Monday November 30th. Meanwhile the U18s face arch-enemies Liverpool on Saturday November 28th, 24 hours before the first team derby on Sunday.

title: Rangers Legend Tips Big-Name Manager for Celtic Job
summary: The Rangers legend has tipped the big-name manager to be interested in the Celtic job.
content: It does feel like the managerial situation has settled down a bit at Celtic over the past few weeks, even though there are still serious question marks over the long-term future of Martin O'Neill. Ideally, one would like to see O'Neill at least finish the season at Celtic. But beyond that, it is hard to see him continuing as manager of the club. Of course, that means that sooner or later, Celtic will need to find themselves a new manager, and hopefully, a long-term one. Quite a few names have been bouncing around in the media as potential solutions to the club's current needs. Could a former Celtic player be the solution? Ally McCoist tips Premier League manager for Celtic job Celtic do have a habit of hiring those with a past with the club. Neil Lennon, Brendan Rodgers and O'Neill all fall under that category. David Moyes is someone whose past with the club dates farther back than any of those three though. It was in 1980 that he broke through the ranks at Celtic as a player. Now, could a return be on the cards as a manager? Rangers legend, Ally McCoist, seems to believe that such a move could be a possibility. As reported by Glasgow World , he said on talkSPORT: “I think the Celtic job would be of interest to him (than Scotland), having played there. I genuinely don’t know what is going on in David’s head, but I would think that job might appeal to him more than the Scotland job. "You could argue that the Scotland job would be the one that everyone wants, being a Scotsman, but he could look around and look at the squad at this time and I’m not sure it would be a massive encouragement to him. He is definitely more hands on, he would struggle to fill his day, David.” Celtic Make Final Decision on January Transfer Move Celtic have already made a final decision amid rumours of a January transfer move. Would David Moyes be the right manager for Celtic? Moyes is one of the managers who has been linked heavily with the Celtic job in recent times. And someone of his experience and calibre would be a welcome addition. Moyes is someone who has a habit of overdelivering with what is presented to him. Right now, he has Everton sitting 9th in the Premier League. Before his arrival, the club had spent several years barely avoiding relegation, often taking it down to the wire. Before that, Moyes had delivered Conference League success at West Ham United and gotten them European football more than once. Since the Scotsman's departure, the Hammers have been relegated to the Championship. Moyes was fantastic during his first stint at Everton as well, a run that lasted over a decade and earned him the chance to be the successor to Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United. Obviously, that did not work out. But having seen a long list of high-profile managers fail after him at Manchester United, it is quite clear that the problems were much deeper than what Moyes was capable of. At the end of the day, if Celtic were able to bring in Moyes, it would have the potential to be an excellent appointment, given he is backed by the board.

title: A Thanksgiving thank you from your local sportswriter | Richards
summary: The stories are great. The people behind them are better. A Thanksgiving thank you to the Lenawee County sports community.
content: It always seems like a great idea. “Alright, everybody, let’s go around the dinner table and each share what we’re thankful for.” On the surface, it’s a lighthearted icebreaker that brings family and friends together to commemorate the start of the holiday season. In practice, it’s a ruthless mind game that feeds on the social anxieties lying beneath our cheerful exteriors. “Family,” the first person says, a layup. The next in line follows suit with another gimme, “Friends.” By this point, the wholesome answers have come to an end, and the jokes start rolling in. “This big ol’ turkey,” the third person chimes in, prompting a chuckle from the other participants in the annual ritual. When it reaches the fourth person, a nervous response follows: “All of this yummy food,” they say. At this point, family, friends and food are off the table. The big three have already been swooped up and we’re only through four people. Obviously, there’s no repeating. It’s the unspoken rule that everyone knows. I’m next. Of course there’s plenty to be thankful for, but at a moment like this nothing comes to mind. All I can hear is a single question racing through my head like static on a dead television channel — “What am I thankful for?” Fortunately, this year, I already know my answer. Three months ago, I started my job as the sports editor for The Daily Telegram in Adrian. It's been a whirlwind of a fall, and while I've spent plenty of time writing stories, compiling stats and emailing coaches, I haven't been able to properly acknowledge the people who have made the last three months possible. So, this Thanksgiving, I'd like to take a moment to do so on behalf of all local sportswriters. To athletic directors: Thank you for putting up with our copious amounts of emails. Keeping tabs on one sport is difficult enough, but overseeing numerous programs and hundreds of student-athletes makes you invaluable resources for writers and equally important figures in your respective schools. To coaches: Thank you for carving time out of your busy schedules to talk to us. For many of you, coaching comes on top of a full-time job as a teacher. Despite the demands on your time, you remain committed role models to your athletes, teaching lessons that extend well beyond the playing field. To student-athletes: Thank you for sharing your stories. Whether it's a quick postgame interview or a longer conversation about your journey, you give us stories worth telling. Your willingness to let us share a small piece of your lives with the community is something writers don't take for granted. And lastly, to our readers: Thank you for supporting local sports coverage. In a world increasingly dominated by algorithms, artificial intelligence and fleeting social media posts, you still make time for stories on those in your community. Whether through the mail slot or on your screens, you welcome our work into your homes. And in doing so, you remind us that there's still value in telling human stories. title: Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027
summary: Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027.
content: In 2025, Oliver Bearman outscored his team-mate Estaban Ocon by three points. This season, he scored three times the points of Ocon before the Frenchman was dropped during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend [Getty Images] Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027. The US-based team announced the 21-year-old's new deal on Thursday, at the start of the Qatar Grand Prix weekend. It marks Bearman's third full season with Haas, for whom he first raced for two one-off events in 2024 before becoming a full-time driver in 2025. The announcement ends a protracted negotiation period in which Bearman's management were seeking reassurances about his future from Ferrari. Bearman is a member of the Italian team's driver academy and has ambitions to race for Ferrari in the future. It was not immediately clear what reassurances Bearman had been given about his future by Ferrari. Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Camara to continue with Haas for final two races Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward." Bearman added: "It's no secret that I'm delighted to be continuing with Haas into 2027. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Bearman will be partnered at Haas next season with Brazilian Rafael Camara, who is also a member of the Ferrari driver academy. Camara has started racing for Haas at the end of this season, following the team's sacking of Frenchman Esteban Ocon midway through the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend. Bearman's concerns about his future had been rooted in the fact that there might not be a seat available at Ferrari for some considerable time. Charles Leclerc is on a long-term contract there, and while Lewis Hamilton's deal is believed to end after 2027, the seven-time champion is keen to continue in F1 for a number more years. Bearman, who said at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, that he was "quite disappointed" his new contract had not yet been sorted so late in the season, is believed to have been exploring his options. His management is said to have been asking Ferrari for reassurances about his future, either about the possibility of racing for the main team, or if that is not an option, being allowed to pursue a career at a more competitive team than Haas. That could eventually lead to a full-time role with Ferrari in the future if Lewis Hamilton or Charles Leclerc leaves. Ferrari is Haas' engine supplier and the two teams have a technical partnership. Câmara is also a Ferrari junior. Bearman, who was 18 at the time, became the third-youngest driver in F1 when he made his debut for Ferrari as a late stand-in at the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in 2024. Then in Formula 2, he also stepped in for Haas later that year before joining the American team on a permanent basis for 2025. title: Botham back as Morgan-Williams to make first start
summary: Wales flanker James Botham is recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan.
content: James Botham and Reuben Morgan-Williams were part of the Wales squad that beat New Zealand [Getty Images/Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales flanker James Botham has been recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. In the only backline alteration for the game in Twickenham, Ospreys scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams will make his first Wales start, with Tomos Williams named among the replacements. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins will captain the side for the first time in more than two years with regular skipper Dewi Lake and flanker Jac Morgan also dropping to the bench. Prop Rhys Carre and hooker Ryan Elias make their first starts of the November campaign, while lock Adam Beard returns at the expense of Ben Carter. Wales have named an experienced bench that includes 294 caps. Botham back after missing Australia Botham produced a player-of-the-match display in the 35-28 victory against New Zealand after making 30 tackles but was left out of the 29-26 defeat by Australia in favour of Cardiff colleague Alex Mann. It was a decision which Botham’s father Liam, himself a former Cardiff wing, said Tandy had got wrong. “I know there's a lot been spoken about it,” said Tandy. “Everyone has got their opinions and people generally tell you who should be in the team and they never tell you who shouldn't. “We're a tight group and as a coach I make sure I speak to all the players before if they are not selected. There'll be reasons why, whether it be bigger picture or whether it is form. “I'll always speak to those, that's a special thing and the connection we feel in our environment.” Botham, who became a father earlier this week, will play at open-side flanker against Japan after starring at blind-side against the All Blacks, with Mann and number eight Aaron Wainwright completing the back row. “James was outstanding against the All Blacks, but we've got a back row depth there that we can move things around and freshen things up," said Tandy. “James has had his little one, he's coming back in full of energy. We were so pleased for him things have gone well there." Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0 Chance for Morgan-Williams to shine at nine Ospreys number nine Morgan-Williams is preparing for his first start in a position that has been dominated by Saracens scrum-half Williams during the Tandy era. Williams has started 14 out of the 15 internationals, including the previous 11, with opportunities in short supply for others. But Williams came off early in the second half against Australia with a groin problem. Carre, named Welsh rugby writers player of the 2025-26 season, is given his first start this autumn, with Nicky Smith dropping out of the squad. Saracens loose-head Carre missed the first month of the season because of a hamstring injury and his only appearance of the autumn Tests so far was off the bench against Japan. Elias, a replacement in the three previous November internationals, is handed his first Test start since the 2024 Six Nations match against France. Montpellier lock Beard returns after missing the loss to Australia after suffering a shoulder injury against New Zealand. Scarlets wing Ellis Mee is given his first involvement in the campaign after being named as a replacement. Tandy has settled on his backline with full-back Blair Murray, wing Louis Rees-Zammit, centres Eddie James and Max Llewellyn and fly-half Sam Costelow starting all four matches in the November campaign as well as prop Archie Griffin and Jenkins. Uncapped quartet Che Hope, Macs Page, Rhys Barratt and Aneurin Owen are among the players who will not be given game time. Wales have won three and lost three of their six Nations Championship matches to finish fifth in the northern hemisphere group, a position matched by Japan in the southern hemisphere section. Wales will face Eddie Jones’ Japan side for a fifth time inside two years with Wales winning three out of the four games. It is the first match of a Saturday double-header, with England and New Zealand to follow. “We were frustrated and disappointed with losing last weekend,” said Tandy. “We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been but there were a lot of positives in the performance to take also. “We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan." title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus.
content: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack. Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus. Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format. Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket. Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approach Sooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers. Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir. "We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel. "The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added. 'This is another level' Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it. "What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said. Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle. "I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded. 136184442

title: Wales make five changes for Japan finale as Rhys Carre earns recall
summary: Wales will look to improve on their narrow win in their first meeting with Japan in the Nations Championship
content: Head coach Steve Tandy has made five alterations to his Wales team for the Nations Championship finale against Japan , recalling loosehead prop Rhys Carre. The Saracens forward was named Wales player of the year in September after an outstanding 2026 Six Nations campaign, but is yet to make a Test start this autumn. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins assumes the captaincy with Dewi Lake named on the bench, while Ryan Elias comes in to start at hooker. Adam Beard partners Jenkins in the second row as James Botham makes his return as openside flanker. Botham was player of the match during Wales’ landmark victory against New Zealand – their first since 1953 – but was left out for last weekend’s defeat to Australia . Scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams makes his full Test debut, with Tomos Williams among the replacements despite having started 14 of Tandy's 15 matches, including the last 11 consecutively. Wales have been much improved in this Nations Championship (Reuters) Wales ended up fifth in the northern hemisphere table of the inaugural Nations Championship after being edged out 29-26 by Australia in Cardiff. They now face southern hemisphere fifth-placed side Japan at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham , on Saturday to determine ninth and 10th position in the competition. Tandy said: "We were frustrated and disappointed with losing last weekend. We probably weren’t as accurate as we could have been. "But there were a lot of positives in the performance to take as well. "We have one more match in this competition on Saturday, away from home. "We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan." title: Jacob Campsey's returns home and revives Devine's football program
summary: Jacob Campsey's returns home and revives Devine's football program with best playoff push since 2011.
content: Members of Devine's football team pose with a banner signifying the Warhorses' 2026 District 14-3A-I championship. (Courtesy/Jacob Campsey) Jacob Campsey proudly strode into San Antonio's Region 20 Education Service Center on Feb. 1 - his first day as Devine's head football coach and athletic director - for UIL's biennial realignment announcement. It was a big one for the Warhorses, who had changed classifications from 4A to 3A, and for Campsey, who was set to take charge at this alma mater 20 years after graduating from there. Everything was new and familiar at the same time. "I have such pride in this brand," Campsey said. "Anytime I put on the ‘DW,' my chest swells up, and that's the honest truth. I feel like the brand represents so many things that are positive in the world, and that's what I love about it." He believes that connection to Devine – a town of 4,700 located about 40 miles south of downtown San Antonio on I-35 - is a big reason why the Warhorses are in the third round of the playoffs for the first time since 2011. "He played for the same team, so I feel there was a better connection between him and the players because he went through all the same stuff we go through," junior running back Enoch Hall said. "He has the experience, and he knows what's right and what's wrong." Jacob Campsey, a 2006 Devine graduate, is in his first season leading his alma mater. The Warhorses are in the third round of the playoffs for the first time since 2011. (Courtesy/Jacob Campsey) Devine (11-1) faces reigning state champion Yoakum (10-2) in a Class 3A Division I regional semifinal at 7 p.m. Friday at Heroes Stadium. The Warhorses earned that opportunity with a come-from-behind victory against Orange Grove last week. Devine trailed by two touchdowns in the first half before staging a big second half for a 49-33 victory. The week before, Devine downed Randolph, 69-21, for its first playoff win since 2015. The Warhorses entered the postseason with 10 straight first round playoffs. "I think it really lit a fire under everybody after we won that first playoff game," junior receiver/defensive back Brody Lane said. "It kind of set everyone's eyes that we could actually go somewhere with this." The Warhorses' run is exactly how Campsey envisioned when he laid out his step-by-step plan to his players in February. Campsey, 38, was hired at Devine after serving as defensive coordinator for three years at Bandera. Campsey pursued the opportunity after Paul Gomez stepped down after nine seasons as Devine's head coach. "Obviously, being home and understanding what the program was about and the foundation that the program had, those opportunities don't come along very often," Campsey said. "It was one of those things that was a no-brainer for me." Before Bandera, Campsey was at Rockdale where he was head coach from 2020-2022 and prior to that, a defensive assistant from 2016-19. Campsey was Rockdale's defensive coordinator in 2017 when the Tigers won the Class 3A Division I state championship. "I had a little bit of an advantage because when you walk in with a state championship ring, there's an immediate buy-in," Campsey said. "They don't have to wonder if it's going to work. The biggest thing was I presented a plan – here are the steps, here's the roadmap , here's what it takes. Here's what we're going to do, and they did it." Devine quarterback Jacob Campsey moves to the outside as Hondo defender Tyler Graff pursues Friday in Hondo. HONDO DEVINE HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL TOM REEL/STAFF NOVEMBER 7, 2003. (TOM REEL/SAN ANTONIO EXPRESS-NEWS) During his playing days, Campsey was a varsity quarterback for Devine for three seasons beginning in 2003. In each of those seasons, the Warhorses when three rounds deep in the postseason. He attended college (but didn't play football) at Mary Hardin-Baylor and got his first assistant job at Thrall when he graduated. After three years there, he went to Rockdale. "Once the whole team saw that he had won a state title and he was really successful in the past few years, it made us all think we were really going to be good," Lane said. It wasn't an easy adjustment. The Warhorses, rooted in the Wishbone since Campsey's playing days, switched to the spread. It was still a run-based offense, but it places an emphasis on getting the ball to their athletes in space. Defensively, the Warhorses went away from a three-man front. Without the benefit of spring practice, the Warhorses made the most of their allotted time during athletic period when they were allowed to run football drills in T-shirts and shorts. They called it their "Breakfast Club" workouts where between 80 and 85 athletes showed up at 6:30 a.m. "That allowed us to get ahead of the curve on some things we were changing schematically," Campsey said. The Warhorses have benefited. Hall has rushed for 1,859 yards and 31 touchdowns on 221 carries. Sophomore Nathan Valle has passed for 2,045 yards and 29 touchdowns. Lane has caught 49 passes for 1,103 yards and 19 touchdowns. A season ago, Hall rushed for 1,329 yards and 18 touchdowns in 11 games. As a team, the Warhorses threw for 1,327 yards and 13 scores. After dropping its season opener against San Diego, 39-21, Devine has reeled off 11 straight wins. They haven't won 11 game in a season since 2011 when it went 13-1 and made it to the state quarterfinals. Devine went 7-0 in 14-3A-I to win its first district championship since 2022. "Everything was new and we definitely had to get used to it," Lane said. "From that first game against San Diego, we've really embraced it. Since that first loss, we've been going through everything with a great mindset that we really wanted to do this (get far in the playoffs) as a team." title: Michigan State Could Be Walking Into a Thanksgiving Upset Against Arkansas as 5.5 Point Underdogs
summary: DETROIT — No. 11 Michigan State (5-1) will have another difficult test on Thanksgiving Day. This time, the Spartans must contend with an Arkansas team capable of making things uncomfortable. content: Nov 17, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks head coach John Calipari at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images DETROIT — No. 11 Michigan State (5-1) will have another difficult test on Thanksgiving Day. This time, the Spartans must contend with an Arkansas team capable of making things uncomfortable. The Arkansas Razorbacks (4-2) will meet the Spartans at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. Tipoff is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. ET on CBS. On paper, Michigan State enters as the favorite. However, Arkansas has enough offensive talent to make this a considerably closer matchup. Arkansas Has Plenty of Offensive Firepower Head coach John Calipari has assembled a young roster with considerable scoring potential. The Razorbacks are averaging 83.5 points through their first six games. Three players have established themselves as particularly important offensive contributors. Billy Richmond III leads Arkansas with 15.0 points per game, followed by Jeremiah Wilkinson at 14.7. Freshman guard Davion Thompson has also emerged as an important piece. He averages 11.3 points and 6.5 assists per game. Thompson recently delivered 13 points and 11 assists against Mississippi Valley State. His ability to create opportunities could become particularly important against Michigan State’s experienced backcourt. Meanwhile, Wilkinson is coming off an impressive shooting performance. He buried eight 3-pointers and finished with 28 points in Arkansas’ 92-48 victory. The Razorbacks have also shown they can compete against quality opposition. They pushed Indiana to an 81-76 finish before falling short on Nov. 17. Michigan State Has Its Own Challenges Michigan State has already demonstrated why it belongs among the country’s best teams. The Spartans defeated then-No. 2 Duke, 79-73, in the Champions Classic. However, Tom Izzo’s team suffered a 61-46 defeat against Tennessee. That performance exposed some offensive concerns heading into Thanksgiving. The Spartans responded with a 91-70 victory over Detroit Mercy. Jeremy Fears Jr. recorded 17 points and 14 assists in the win. Fears has been one of college basketball’s most productive floor generals. He averages 16.7 points and 9.3 assists per game. That presents a difficult assignment for Arkansas. Containing Fears and limiting his ability to create opportunities will be critical. Michigan State also has a considerable advantage on the glass. The Spartans rank among the nation’s better rebounding teams and have consistently generated second-chance opportunities. Arkansas cannot afford to give Michigan State extra possessions. That could quickly turn a competitive game into a comfortable Spartans victory. Calipari Knows What Awaits Him There is also some familiarity between these programs. Calipari and Izzo have developed a longstanding relationship through their coaching careers. Michigan State defeated Arkansas 69-66 in East Lansing last November. The Razorbacks will have an opportunity to return the favor in a much different environment. Calipari knows the physical challenge that comes with playing Izzo’s teams. “You’re playing Michigan State, it’s going to be roughhouse basketball,” Calipari told CBS Sports’ Jon Rothstein. That assessment could define Thursday’s matchup. Arkansas must match Michigan State’s physicality while maintaining its offensive rhythm. The Razorbacks also enter with a young roster. Handling adversity against an experienced opponent will be another important test. Michigan State could receive a boost from the expected returns of Coen Carr and Jordan Scott. Both starters missed the Spartans’ most recent game with injuries. Izzo said he expected both players to return against Arkansas. However, their availability and potential workloads remained dependent on their recovery. An Opportunity for an Arkansas Statement Arkansas has lost both of its matchups against high-major competition this season. Those defeats came against Virginia and Indiana. Consequently, Thursday represents an important opportunity for Calipari’s program. Beating a top-15 opponent would provide an early-season statement. Michigan State certainly has the experience and defensive discipline to avoid an upset. Still, Arkansas has enough offensive production to challenge the Spartans. The Razorbacks will need strong performances from Richmond, Wilkinson and Thompson. They must also limit turnovers and compete on the offensive glass. A victory would give Arkansas one of its most meaningful results of the young season. It would also give the program momentum heading into its upcoming SEC-ACC Challenge matchup against North Carolina. Michigan State and Arkansas meet Thursday, Nov. 26, at 4:30 p.m. ET. The Thanksgiving showdown will air nationally on CBS.

content: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Stephen Curry is set for a crucial injury re-evaluation as the Golden State Warriors look for clarity on when their superstar could return to action. The four-time NBA champion has been sidelined since suffering an oblique abdominal tear during the Warriors’ 115-108 defeat to the Houston Rockets. According to ESPN’s Anthony Slater, Curry will undergo his next medical assessment as Golden State continue to navigate life without their leading scorer. Stephen Curry injury update gives Golden State Warriors important recovery checkpoint Curry suffered the injury early against Houston, leaving the game with 6:25 remaining in the first quarter after experiencing discomfort in his right abdominal area. An MRI subsequently confirmed an oblique tear, with the Warriors initially ruling him out for at least two weeks. Friday’s re-evaluation will offer a clearer picture of his recovery, although it does not automatically mean he will be cleared to return. Before his injury, Curry was enjoying another excellent campaign, averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.7 rebounds across 10 games. He was also shooting 50 per cent from the field and 45.7 per cent from three-point range. His absence has exposed just how much Golden State rely on his offensive production, with Steve Kerr admitting the team need to make adjustments. Speaking on the Tom Tolbert Show, the Warriors coach acknowledged that their previous approach placed too much responsibility on Curry. “We’ve recognized that the way we were running our offense was too Steph-dependent, and so we’ve tweaked a few things,” Kerr said. The numbers underline that problem, with Golden State recording a plus/minus of +45.5 per game with Curry this season compared to -53.8 without him. The Warriors have also been without Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, while Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away from basketball because of an illness. Golden State did manage to beat the Boston Celtics 88-87 after a difficult five-game road losing streak, but they still need Curry back if they are to compete consistently in the Western Conference. His assessment should provide an important indication of the next stage of his recovery, with the Warriors keen to avoid rushing their franchise cornerstone back before he is ready. title: Detroit Lions picks vs Bears: Who'll come out on top on Thanksgiving?
summary: Will the Detroit Lions keep their six-game win streak going against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving? Six Free Press sports writers make their picks.
content: Grab a turkey leg – no turducken, since this game’s on CBS, not Fox – and settle in for the Detroit Lions ’ 87 th Thanksgiving Day game, as they host the Chicago Bears on Thursday, Nov. 26. The 1 p.m. start will mark the 21 st meeting between the Lions and Bears on Turkey Day (second behind only the 23 games between the Lions and Packers ), with the Bears owning an 11-9 edge in the holiday series (and a 3-2 edge at Ford Field on the holiday). Still, the Lions had the edge the last time they met on Thanksgiving, with a 23-20 win in 2024, and have beaten former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson’s squad in both reunions since. MAN IN THE MIDDLE: Lions will see whole new Bears defense in Thanksgiving game thanks to Jeffery Simmons Will the Lions keep that streak, not to mention their six-game win streak this season, going? Six Free Press sports writers make their picks: Detroit Lions predictions vs Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Dave Birkett In their long Thanksgiving history, the Lions haven't played many games bigger than this. The Lions and Bears are two of the three best teams in the NFC with identical 8-2 records and similar playing styles. The Lions are at home and have the best running back in football. The Bears are healthier and still riding the euphoria of their big trade deadline acquisition. In a game between two evenly matched teams, I see this one coming down to who has the ball last. The pick: Bears 31, Lions 30. Carlos Monarrez I’ve written that I won’t pick the Lions to lose again, until they finally do. But this one’s tough to resist. These teams are both 8-2, but the Lions have taken advantage of the NFL’s easiest strength of schedule, while the Bears have battled through the NFL’s hardest strength of schedule – and scored 34 against Seattle’s top-ranked defense. I’ve giving the Lions this game purely on homefield advantage. The pick: Lions 32, Bears 25 (OT). Christian Romo Don't expect to glean anything meaningful from the result of this game. Both of these teams are playing on a short week in front of a national audience, with the Lions missing their two best defensive players and the Bears 0-2 vs. the Lions under Johnson. The Lions could get blown out and still end up winning the division, while the Bears could put up a stinker and still be Super Bowl favorites. The Jan. 3 rematch in Chicago will probably come with real stakes – hello again, NBC? – but consider this one a midseason exhibition between two teams with similar résumés and a strong desire to enjoy a long weekend. The Bears are favored by less than a field goal because many consider them to be one of the two best teams in the NFC (along with the 9-1 San Francisco 49ers). But Detroit has done nothing but exceed expectations over the last six games, so why not make it a seventh? The pick: Lions 28, Bears 27. Rainer Sabin The last time Ben Johnson visited Ford Field, the Lions humiliated the Bears in his second game as head coach. Johnson certainly remembers that 52-21 beatdown delivered by the same organization that served as the launchpad for his career ascent from quality control coach to wunderkind play-caller. Johnson will be eager to finally exact revenge in this pivotal divisional showdown, and he now has superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to support his mission. Simmons gives Chicago the edge in this matchup and helps Johnson earn his first victory against his former team in a game that goes down to the wire. The pick: Bears 27, Lions 24. Jeff Seidel This is going to be an absolutely wild, fascinating, and incredibly important game. And it comes at the perfect time for the Lions because they have been playing tremendous football. Sure, Ben Johnson will bring out some wrinkles and find some creative ways to score. He certainly knows this coaching staff, these players and this scheme. But he will end up overthinking it and go back to the Windy City with his third straight loss to his mentor. All of that, plus, more than anything, it’s at home for the Lions. The pick: Lions 31, Bears 28. Shawn Windsor Jeffery Simmons has five sacks in three games since joining Chicago and turned the Bears into the most complete team in the NFC North ... so far. His answer focused on what a potential employer would have to consider after watching Pittsburgh’s situation unravel. Co-panelist Michael Irvin also weighed in and added, “How do you bring Aaron in when you’re seeing how this is ending, and if it doesn’t work out for you and your club, you can imagine it’s going to end like this, Aaron Rodgers on Pat McAfee and all of these things.” Matthews and Irvin were offering their assessment of Rodgers’ market. They did not identify a team that had rejected the quarterback or announce that Rodgers had retired. The concern is another possibility of another public breakup. For a franchise weighing a late-season quarterback addition, Matthews believes the way this relationship ended could be difficult to overlook. Meanwhile, Irvin made it clear that he appreciated the quarterback’s place in NFL history, calling him “one of the greatest quarterbacks we’ve ever had in this National Football League.” “For him to end his career like this, walking off the football field like this, that’s very sad,” Irvin futher added. Steelers Move Forward With Mason Rudolph After Rodgers’ Release Pittsburgh officially released Rodgers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, after announcing the previous night that Mason Rudolph would start against Denver on Black Friday. The change came with the Steelers at 6-4. Rodgers then delivered a scathing assessment of McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show” , including allegations about the coach sleeping during meetings and failing to prepare adequately. Those comments helped turn a quarterback change into a much wider examination of Pittsburgh’s leadership. McCarthy subsequently said the benching followed an ultimatum from Rodgers that fell outside a player’s responsibilities. His comments effectively asked a prospective team to consider how a reunion or fresh start might end if expectations went unmet. Pittsburgh has already chosen Rudolph for its next game. Rodgers’ next opportunity depends on another team either claiming him off waivers or, if he clears, deciding he is worth a free-agent deal. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Jayden Daniels: Brandon Aiyuk and I put the past behind us
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media.
content: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media. After Aiyuk signed with the Commanders this week, however, Daniels said that's all behind them. "I'm a grown man, he's a grown man," Daniels said. "Things happen. You don't know what he was going through. You don't know what I was going through at that time." Daniels said he looked up to Aiyuk when they were at Arizona State together and thinks they can have a good relationship as teammates again. "That's somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU," Daniels said. "So, like I said, I know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle our differences and just move forward from there. That's like a brother to me. Like I said, we've been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, just put the past behind us." As for the social media posts that Aiyuk made, Daniels said he was never angry about that. "I prayed for him because he's like family to me," Daniels said. "I think that was a very dark moment in his life." Daniels declined to go into specifics about recent conversations with Aiyuk but said he hopes Aiyuk will be a good addition to the Commanders. "That's between us, personal, but yeah, we did chat," Daniels said. "He works hard. Before his knee injury he was All-Pro, very explosive, big catch radius, so excited for him to have a fresh start, new opportunity to prove himself day in and day out." Aiyuk hasn't played in more than two years, but he was once one of the best receivers in the NFL. If Aiyuk can play at anything close to the level he used to play at, he can be a significant addition to the Commanders' offense. Daniels is excited about that possibility.

title: Jayden Daniels talks how he repaired relationship with Brandon Aiyuk
summary: Jayden Daniels reveals how he and new teammate Brandon Aiyuk repaired their relationship.
content: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk are close. They became friends back in 2019, when Daniels was a freshman quarterback at Arizona State, and Aiyuk was a receiver. They’ve remained close over the years, and when Aiyuk was going through contract negotiations with the San Francisco 49ers in 2024, he hinted at potentially reuniting with Daniels in Washington. After injuring his knee in Oct. 2024, Aiyuk later feuded with the 49ers. Earlier this year, he aired his grievances on social media, and even donned Commanders’ gear. Aiyuk made it clear he wanted to play for Washington, reportedly even buying a home in Northern Virginia. But amid those numerous social media videos over the summer, he even took aim at Daniels and his mother, who represents the quarterback as his agent. The friendship seemingly cooled and reports out of Washington indicated that the Commanders were no longer a possibility for Aiyuk if he were released. However, ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Daniels and Aiyuk had patched up their differences. Earlier this month, Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus as his agent, applied for NFL reinstatement (the 49ers had him on the reserve/left squad list), and on Monday, he finally got his wish as the 49ers released him. The Commanders were linked to Aiyuk as soon as he was released. On Thursday, the two sides made it official, with Aiyuk joining Washington’s practice squad . Daniels met with the media on Thursday and was asked about how he repaired his relationship with Aiyuk. “I mean, I’m a grown man, he’s a grown man,” Daniels said. “Things happen, I don’t, and you don’t know what he was going through. You don’t know what I was going through at that time. So, he just sit up there. That’s somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU and stuff like that. So, like I said, I kinda know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle it out set our differences and kinda just move forward from there. That’s, it’s a brother to me. Like I said, we’ve been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, kinda just put the past behind us.” It’s good that Daniels and Aiyuk repaired things. Now, Aiyuk will have to win over an entire locker room, as there will undoubtedly be some questions about him. “He’s gotta prove to the locker room the type of guy he is, his character, high-character guy, stuff like that. So, it’ll be fun, but it’ll be a process.” There are no guarantees for Aiyuk. He must be on his best behavior to eventually win a spot on Washington’s 53-man roster. But it’s good to have the quarterback on your side. This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Jayden Daniels talks how he repaired relationship with Brandon Aiyuk

title: NFL insider shares anonymous Steelers players’ replies to Aaron Rodgers’ Mike McCarthy comments
