title: Rams aren't the Super Bowl team we expected -- they're better
summary: The Rams that were supposed to win the Super Bowl lost their stars and don't exist anymore. The team that replaced them might just be more dominant.
content: The Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) scores a touchdown during an NFL football game against The Green Bay Packers on November 25th, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- The Rams were supposed to win the Super Bowl with Matthew Stafford throwing to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams in one of the highest scoring offenses in football. Nacua is done for the season. Adams hasn't played since October. Stafford threw for 140 yards on Wednesday night. And the Rams pushed the Green Bay Packers around and controlled the clock for 40 minutes and 40 seconds. The Rams; 26-13 win on Thanksgiving Eve was their fifth straight, and for the first time this season, the Rams would be in the playoffs if the season ended today. That would have sounded like a modest goal in August, when they were the prohibitive Super Bowl favorites. But the team that carried those expectations never took the field all at once, and it doesn't exist anymore. What exists now is something Sean McVay has never coached before: a team that runs the ball 45 times, wins time of possession by more than 20 minutes and dares you to do something about it. Nobody has yet. The Rams' injury list reads like a depth chart of a preseason favorite. Nacua and cornerback Jaylen Watson are done for the season after seven games. Defensive tackle Poona Ford is done after six, and tight end Terrance Ferguson after three. Starting interior offensive linemen Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton have been out since starting the first nine games. Adams, Avila and Shelton are all expected back at some point, but the Rams know the roster will likely be a revolving door, with players seemingly going down each time they take the field. On Wednesday, the Rams lost tight end Davis Allen and offensive lineman Bill Murray, who will be reevaluated this week. The Rams' injury woes began around the time they lost to the lowly Arizona Cardinals at home to fall to 2-4 on Oct. 18. They haven't lost since. Despite the injuries, they have reeled off five straight wins to improve to 7-4, the same record they had through 11 games the last time they won the Super Bowl. If the Rams hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy at SoFi Stadium at the end of this season, they will do it as a completely different team than the one that began it. McVay has been forced to abandon his traditional pass-heavy identity and lean into a physical, ball-control style that looks more like Bill Parcells' 1990 New York Giants than any of McVay's high-octane teams. Most of the promotional material heading into this season featured Nacua and Adams. But if the Rams make the playoffs, it will be because they have one of the league's best rushing attacks, averaging more than 142 rushing yards per game behind Blake Corum (731 yards, 5.4 yards per carry) and Kyren Williams (662 yards, seven touchdowns). Against Green Bay, the Rams ran for 241 yards, including 184 on 32 carries from Corum. The Rams ran 71 plays to Green Bay's 44. That's the 1990 Giants' Super Bowl XXV blueprint, nearly to the second. According to OptaStats, only twice in the 21st century has an NFL team run the ball 30 or more times in the second half, piled up 145 or more rushing yards, held the ball for at least 23 minutes and allowed zero points. Both were by the Rams in the last 11 days. For all the talk about the Rams' running backs, the defense has carried this team during the winning streak. The Rams have held four of their last five opponents to 13 points or fewer, including the Chargers to nine, the Cardinals to six and the Packers to 13. They haven't allowed a rushing touchdown in six straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL. They have held opponents under 65 rushing yards in four straight games, which is also the longest active streak in the league. They have allowed four touchdowns in their last six games. And they haven't allowed a first-quarter touchdown in 12 straight games dating to last season, a franchise record. Nate Landman forced a fumble, his eighth as a Ram and the most in the NFL since he arrived in 2025. Jaylen McCollough and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. intercepted Jordan Love, giving the Rams eight different players with an interception this season, the most in the league. Kobie Turner returned after five weeks on injured reserve as the Rams honored the legendary "Fearsome Foursome" by wearing their iconic blue and white uniforms and unleashing theitr modern day version led by Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, Byron Young an Turner. For the first time this season all five core pass rushers for the Rams took the field together. The most damning thing about Wednesday night from Green Bay's perspective is that the Packers knew exactly what was coming and still couldn't stop it. "Our inability to stop the run, which is exactly what we knew that they were going to try to do, that's a recipe for disaster," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. "And tonight it was." That's what an identity looks like. It isn't a trick that works once. It works even when the other side knows it's coming. For nearly a decade, McVay has been the NFL's most imitated offensive mind, the play-action, pre-snap motion, make-the-defense-guess architect who turned unknown receivers into All-Pros. This version of McVay is running the ball 45 times and daring you to stop it. The Rams have run for 200-plus yards in back-to-back games for the first time since 1984, when Eric Dickerson was setting the single-season rushing record. Over the last five games, they've outrushed opponents 895-261. Last week, they closed out the game with a 12-minute, 15-second drive. "The game honors toughness," McVay said. "I think we're playing tougher. … It's almost like body blows. As the game goes on, those hit a little bit harder than maybe they do earlier on in the game, and that's when you're able to get 45 carries off." Corum spent his birthday putting together one of the best rushing performances in franchise history. His 184 yards were the most by a Ram since Todd Gurley ran for 208 in 2018, and according to ESPN, they were the second-most by a player on his birthday in NFL history, behind only Bo Jackson's 221 in 1987. He was the first Ram with 30 carries in a game since Gurley in 2015, and he has scored a touchdown in seven straight games. Williams added a rushing touchdown of his own, the 43rd of his career, tying Dan Towler for fifth in franchise history. They did it behind an offensive line that was being rebuilt during the game. With Avila and Shelton already out, David Quessenberry, Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich all rotated in, with tight ends Colby Parkinson and Max Klare playing all over the formation. "We were able to control the line of scrimmage," Stafford said, "which was the recipe for success today." Stafford, playing in his 250th career regular-season start (just the sixth quarterback in NFL history to reach that mark), completed 16 of 23 passes for 140 yards and an interception. A year ago, that line would have been a crisis. Now it's a supporting role, and Stafford seems fine with it. "Some weeks it's handing the ball off a bunch of times," Stafford said. "Other weeks it's throwing the ball a little bit more. We're playing as a team right now." That's the real reason the Rams are still Super Bowl contenders, just not for the reasons anyone expected in August. This team doesn't need any one star. A ball-control offense and a defense that won't let you run travel well in January, when the weather turns and the margins shrink. And the reinforcements are coming. Think about what this offense looks like when Adams comes back to a defense that's already slanting fronts and sending defensive backs at the line just to slow down the run game, and when Avila and Shelton return to a line that has learned how to win without them. Is there a concern? Of course. The passing game is the question nobody in that locker room is pretending to have answered. If the Rams fall behind by two scores in a playoff game, can a team built to win 26-13 win 34-31? Stafford knows it, too. "There are some opportunities for us to be better and cleaner, especially in the pass game," he said, "and I'll obviously work to be that for us." The last time the Rams were 7-4, in 2021, they were built for the moment through blockbuster moves: Stafford, Von Miller, Odell Beckham Jr. This team was built by whoever was left standing. McVay quoted his old college coach at Miami (Ohio), Terry Hoeppner, after the game: "Have a plan, work the plan, plan for the unexpected." The Rams that were supposed to win the Super Bowl this season don't exist anymore. The ones that do might be better built to win it.

title: Rams CB Calls Out Refs With 11-Word Message Over Kamren Kinchens’ Controversial Ejection vs. Packers
summary: Kamren Kinchens was sent off for a hit on Christian Watson. Another Los Angeles Rams defensive back, watching from the sidelines with a season-ending injury, had a rather different take on the decision.
content: Rams CB Calls Out Refs With 11-Word Message Over Kamren Kinchens’ Controversial Ejection vs. Packers Kamren Kinchens was sent off for a hit on Christian Watson. Another Los Angeles Rams defensive back, watching from the sidelines with a season-ending injury, had a rather different take on the decision. The Rams safety was ejected during the first half of Wednesday’s Thanksgiving Eve clash against the Green Bay Packers after a collision with wide receiver Watson left him being evaluated for a concussion. The league reviewed the play and ruled that Kinchens had left his feet and made helmet-to-helmet contact. But Jaylen Watson, who is currently on injured reserve, wasn’t buying the decision. The two-time Super Bowl champion took to social media with a pointed message for the officials, questioning whether playing physical defense had become a problem in the NFL. Jaylen Watson Takes Aim at Officials After Kamren Kinchens’ Ejection The Rams and Packers entered their Thanksgiving Eve matchup with identical 6-4 records, making the Netflix showdown an important one in the NFC playoff race. Kinchens’ departure added another complication for Los Angeles, particularly with the secondary already dealing with injuries. The incident happened with 1:54 remaining in the first half. Facing fourth-and-1, Packers quarterback Jordan Love lofted a pass towards Watson, who was tracking the ball near the sideline. Kinchens arrived at full speed and collided with the receiver, making contact around the head and neck area. Watson remained down for several moments before getting up and walking to the locker room for a concussion evaluation. He was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The NFL’s decision to eject Kinchens came from the league office, with executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent making the final call. The reasoning, communicated during the Netflix broadcast, was that the Rams safety had left his feet and made helmet-to-helmet contact. The play also produced an unusual officiating sequence. Kinchens was called for unnecessary roughness, but the penalty was offset by offensive pass interference against Packers receiver Matthew Golden. As a result, Green Bay did not receive an automatic first down, and the down was replayed. Jaylen Watson wasn’t too happy with the ejection issued against Kamren Kinchens for the hit on Packers’ star Christian Watson. It remains to be seen if the NFL retroactively changes the distinction. But for this game, the Rams had to move forward without Kinchens in the lineup. He is ranked 58th in PFN’s Safety Impact Score with a grade of 71.2 entering Week 12. His availability and consistently solid production in the spot have been invaluable to a Rams team already dealing with a ton of injuries. His absence, though, did not derail the side on the night. They forced three turnovers and eventually pulled away for a 26-13 victory, their fifth consecutive win. The result moved Los Angeles to 7-4, while Green Bay fell to 6-5. title: Rashee Rice addresses preparation for the Bills' physical defense

title: Four-time MVP Rodgers released and may have played last NFL game
summary: Aaron Rodgers is replaced as the Pittsburgh Steelers' starting quarterback, then criticises head coach Mike McCarthy before being released with immediate effect.
content: Aaron Rodgers has thrown 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions from 10 games this season [Getty Images] Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. In a brief statement published on Wednesday afternoon local time, the Steelers announced Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, was no longer with the franchise. That came after a tumultuous 24 hours, which began with the Steelers announcing at 23:10 local time on Tuesday that Rodgers had been replaced as their starting quarterback. He then appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, saying he would not rejoin the team. "That ship has sailed," said Rodgers, who turns 43 next week. During the 34-minute interview, he said he discovered he had been replaced from team-mate Pat Freiermuth. Rodgers was also critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings. They won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2011 and, during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers said that McCarthy ended the half-time huddle with a chant of "one, two, three, Packers". When asked by reporters on Wednesday about that claim, McCarthy admitted there was "an embarrassing moment". The 63-year-old was in charge for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell with the Packers and left in 2018. He then coached the Dallas Cowboys from 2020-2024. Tension had developed between the pair over play-calling and Rodgers said he told McCarthy "try to bench me or don't change the play-caller, then you should just release me". McCarthy later said "there was an ultimatum made that was clearly outside his job description", adding it was his decision to let the player go. All this came after the Steelers said that Mason Rudolph will start Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos and that Rodgers would be inactive, so would not serve as back-up to the 31-year-old. Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets, was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs. McCarthy's appointment persuaded him to play one more year but Rodgers told the talk show on Wednesday the season had not been "what I signed up for". Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have had two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at Philadelphia on Sunday. Analysis - an unceremonious end to an illustrious career? Pittsburgh's brief statement confirming Rodgers' release is likely the unceremonious end to an illustrious career. While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win with Green Bay, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times. Rodgers had said his 22nd year in the NFL would be his last, and he has been let go at a crucial stage in the season. The Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) lead the AFC North division, with Pittsburgh third, but with seven games left the Steelers occupy the final play-off spot for the AFC Conference. Although Pittsburgh are 6-4, they have had to grind out some of those wins as they have struggled offensively. They rank 22nd for both points and passing yards per game. Rodgers is undoubtedly past his best, but his form has only dropped slightly from last season and the team's struggles are by no means entirely down to him. The Steelers' depth among their wide receivers is thin. Michael Pittman is out injured and DK Metcalf has not delivered the production expected when he was brought in with Rodgers before the 2025 season. Metcalf, 28, was even ejected during Sunday's loss at Philadelphia, meaning Rodgers had to lean on debutant Max Hurleman with the game on the line. It is not as if Pittsburgh had a hot-shot rookie quarterback pushing for an opportunity. Rudolph is in his ninth season and has started each as a back-up. But this week's discussions with Rodgers forced McCarthy's hand and the manner in which the situation unraveled cannot be a complete surprise given Rodgers has clashed with team management, coaches and team-mates throughout his career. While McCarthy hopes Rudolph can spark the Steelers' offence, Rodgers is now free to join another team. Several have had quarterback issues this season through injuries and poor form, and with more than a third of it left, there is time for Rodgers - one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time - to come aboard and make an impact. The Indianapolis Colts are one of those teams having released Daniel Jones last week, but they are out of play-off contention. That leaves the New England Patriots as an intriguing alternative. Drake Maye will be out for at least six weeks after suffering a fractured fibula and at 5-5 are just outside the AFC's play-off spots - one below Pittsburgh. The Patriots have Super Bowl pedigree having reached last season's big game and Rodgers would relish the chance to deny McCarthy and his former team. It would also give him the opportunity to follow his former adversary Tom Brady and get one last shot at finally emulating Brady and Manning by becoming a multiple Super Bowl winner himself. title: Pete DeBoer reunites Mathew Barzal with Bo Horvat and it pays off for Islanders
summary: The Islanders’ first crack at remaking their top line after Kyle Palmieri’s injury was going back to an old standby.
content: The Islanders’ first crack at remaking their top line after Kyle Palmieri’s injury was going back to an old standby. Mathew Barzal was on Bo Horvat’s right wing for the first time this season, with Simon Holmstrom to Horvat’s left, as coach Pete DeBoer juggled his lines for Wednesday’s 3-2 shootout win over the Blues . All four lines looked different from the disastrous loss to the Maple Leafs two nights prior. The second line of Emil Heineman, Brayden Schenn and Victor Eklund was reunited. Bo Horvat celebrates after scoring the game-winning shootout goal in the Islanders’ 3-2 win over the Blues on Nov. 25, 2026, at UBS Arena. Corey Sipkin for New York Post Calum Ritchie was at right wing in his first game back in the lineup, completing a third line with Anthony Duclair on the left and Jean-Gabriel Pageau at center. Matias Maccelli was dropped to the fourth line on Casey Cizikas’ right, with Ondrej Palat at left wing. “I liked all our lines tonight,” DeBoer said, with three of the four having a positive shots-for margin on the evening, per Natural Stat Trick. “It wasn’t perfect but that was a really tight-checking game. There wasn’t a lot of room there. … We’ll see going forward but I liked everybody out there tonight.” Horvat and Barzal have played surprisingly little together since the 2023-24 season, when they were mainstays on the Islanders’ top line. Largely due to Barzal’s injury, they had just 18 games on the same line in 2024-25, then just 16 games together last season with both healthy. During nearly 300 minutes together at 5-on-5 last season, though, the pair had a 54.64 expected goals percentage. DeBoer said during an optional pregame skate that the Islanders were still working through possibilities, though their lineup largely mirrored the way they’d practiced Tuesday. The Islanders were still in wait-and-see mode Wednesday morning on Palmieri as he continued to see doctors, but the tone was pessimistic after the winger suffered a right knee injury Monday night. “It’s heartbreaking,” DeBoer said. “Same as [Alexander Romanov], same as what [Ryan Pulock’s] dealing with, really. If you would’ve told me at the 20-game mark that those three guys would all be facing what they’re facing, or faced already, it’s heartbreaking because all three of them went through long summers and rehab, things like that.” Asked whether surgery was a possibility for Palmieri, who tore the ACL in his left knee a year ago, DeBoer said, “I think everything’s on the table. We won’t know until he sees the doctors.” Logan Stanley played Wednesday after missing practice Tuesday for maintenance. Defenseman Kashawn Aitcheson was held out of the lineup in AHL Hamilton on Wednesday as a disciplinary measure because he was late to a treatment appointment, coach Jay McKee told local reporters. The Islanders held a pregame ceremony to honor Cizikas for reaching the 1,000-game mark .

title: Alisson Becomes First LFC Goalkeeper to Register Assist in Champions League History
summary: Still breaking records.
content: Liverpool's goalkeeper #01 Alisson Becker (R) and Liverpool's forward #09 Alexander Isak celebrate at the end of the UEFA Champions League league phase football match between Club Brugge and Liverpool at Jan-Breydel Stadium in Bruges on November 25, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images A rather inexplicable statistic has emerged following Liverpool FC’s 3-0 away win over Club Brugge in the UEFA Champions League. Goalkeeper Alisson Becker hoofed the ball long to Alexander Isak, who went one-on-one with veteran keeper Yann Sommer and scored. That… was somehow the first assist by a Liverpool keeper in the competition’s history. This appears to include European Cup fixtures, and not some Premier League/First Division delineation we’re so used to being subjected to exclude some all-time Liverpool greats from whatever conversations sports media wants us to have. 1 – Alisson is the first Liverpool goalkeeper to provide an assist in the UEFA Champions League. Inventive. pic.twitter.com/1bHLTFuwYC — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) November 25, 2026 Other interesting statistics: This was Alisson’s fourth assist for the club. His previous three? All of them were for one Mohamed Salah. Of course, Alisson also has a goal to his name, with the memorable header in the dying seconds against West Brom seared into everybody’s minds. This assist was almost exactly like those Salah goals, a long, accurate ball, and Isak was off to the races, with only the opposition keeper to beat. The recent news that Alisson is open to an extension should be music to every Liverpool fan’s ears. The club has been blessed with some wonderful goalkeepers, and Alisson could very well be the best of them all with his complete game.

title: Analysing Arsenal ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash

content: Analysing Arsenal ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash A closer look at the side we’ll play this Sunday… Men's Team How can I watch Arsenal v City on TV around the globe? We go to north London to face defending Premier League champions Arsenal in a 16:30 (UK) kick-off. City come into the weekend third in the league, with 22 points from 11 games – having won seven, drawn one and lost three. With the help of Opta data, we find out more about the Arsenal team we’ll play… Recent form Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the table, claiming 28 from a possible 33 so far this season. Their one defeat came against Brighton in September but their only draw was in their last outing – a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United last weekend. They also tied with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday evening. However, they’ve very much enjoyed playing at home in the league this season and remain the only side yet to drop points at their home ground across all 20 sides. Men's Team Register your interest in our new PUMA x C.P. Company kit Preferred lineup Arsenal almost exclusively play 4-2-3-1 under Mikel Arteta. David Raya has established himself as one of the world’s best goalkeepers but could miss this game through injury, with Kepa Arrizabalaga the assumed stand-in. From right to left, Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori appear to be the first choice back four during William Saliba’s injury absence. The likes of Ben White and Piero Hincapie may otherwise feature. In the double pivot, it’s either Bruno Guimaraes or Myles Lewis-Skelly to partner Declan Rice with captain Martin Odegaard ahead of them. Men's Team Maresca: We take the point and move on Noni Madueke has been in form on the right wing with Bukayo Saka currently out, with Christos Tzolis or Eberechi Eze on the left. Kai Havertz is the main man in the No.9 role. Manager Mikel Arteta cut his teeth in the coaching world under Pep Guardiola following his retirement in 2016 until becoming Arsenal boss in December 2019. He ensured gradual improvement, finishing runners-up to City in 2022/23 and 2023/24 before getting their hands on the title last time out. Only two managers currently in the Premier League have overseen more than his 259 games in charge – David Moyes and Mauricio Pochettino – but he is the longest serving manager in his current job by 109 matches. In his 259 Premier League games as boss to date, he’s won 158, drawn 49 and lost 52 times. That means his 61% win rate is by far the best of any manager currently in the competition. One of the current wave of outstanding managers from the Basque country, Arteta is known for a passion and exuberance in the dugout. Head-to-head record Having won on six consecutive Premier League trips to Arsenal between 2018 and 2023, we haven’t been victorious on our last three visits. Overall, the two sides have met 58 times in the Premier League with Arsenal winning 25 and City 20. Seven of our victories have come at Arsenal’s home. Interestingly, we have won 12 of our last 14 Premier League games against reigning champions, completing the double over Liverpool last season. We lost the Community Shield 3-0 to them in August but we did have the upper hand over Arsenal in meetings last season, with a late, late equaliser at the Emirates earning them a point before we won 2-1 at the Etihad in April. How they defend Resolutely. There’s no doubt their defence is what their success last season was built upon. In fact, David Raya has won the last three Premier League Golden Glove awards since moving to Arsenal and is in pole position for this one too. They conceded just 27 times last season and have only let in seven so far more than a quarter of the way through the campaign. That record is again the best in the league so far, while they have the meanest defence inside the box and in the first 15 minutes of games. However, they are a little more susceptible to set pieces than last season with their two goals conceded from corners only putting them mid-table in the Premier League. Only two sides have committed fewer fouls than them so far and seen fewer yellow cards too. How they attack With 17 goals so far, they’re the seventh most prolific side in the division. That matches their place in the table for big chances created (28) and is slightly better than their ninth place for amount of shots (151). They’re nowhere near as threatening from set pieces this season as last, with just two goals from those situations so far. Martin Odegaard is a central figure in everything they do. Since the 2023/24 season, only Bruno Fernandes (41) and Mohamed Salah (35) have more Premier League assists than Odegaard (25). Meanwhile, Kai Havertz has enjoyed playing against us recently having been involved in four goals in our last four games. With 514 passes per match, they are the fifth most possession focused side in the league, with City top on 634. Havertz, Odegaard and Saka all have three goals each, with several others chipping in too. City v Leeds: Tickets on sale now Don’t miss out on our exciting clash with Leeds this December. Enzo Maresca’s men comes up against Daniel Farke’s team on Wednesday 2 December, kick-off 19:30 (UK). Tickets are on sale to Premium, Matchday and Junior Members with one previous purchase at the Etihad Stadium. It’s four tickets per Member with an additional three for Season Ticket Members. title: Andoni Iraola optimistic over Victor Munoz knee injury after Liverpool beat Club Brugge
summary: Andoni Iraola remains optimistic over Victor Munoz's knee injury after the winger limped off during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge. Despite the £34.5 million summer signing leaving the pitch in significant discomfort, the manager offered a hopeful update ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Everton.
content: SOCCER CL DAY5 CLUB BRUGGE VS LIVERPOOL FC - AFP Andoni Iraola remains optimistic over Victor Munoz's knee injury after the winger limped off during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge. Despite the £34.5 million summer signing leaving the pitch in significant discomfort, the manager offered a hopeful update ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Everton. Munoz limps off in Liverpool win Iraola says he remains optimistic regarding Munoz's fitness after the winger was forced off with a knee injury during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League victory over Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The 23-year-old suffered the blow in the closing stages of the first half in Belgium. Although Munoz looked in significant discomfort as he departed, he was able to limp off the pitch without needing a stretcher. His premature exit proved to be the sole concern on an otherwise comfortable European evening for Liverpool, leaving the club waiting anxiously to learn the extent of the damage. Iraola offers hopeful post-match injury update Speaking after the win in Belgium, Iraola admitted that seeing Munoz forced off dampened the mood despite the convincing scoreline. However, the Liverpool boss revealed that the winger's outlook had already improved by the time the match concluded. "It was the worst part of the game, definitely," Iraola said, as quoted by Metro . "He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive after the game had finished. In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game I spoke with him and he was a little bit more optimistic." Liverpool cruise past Brugge despite setback Munoz joined Liverpool in the summer after completing a £34.5 million transfer from Osasuna. The club's medical staff will now evaluate how the joint reacts before determining whether the issue is minor or more serious. "It was a knock on the knee so now we have to assess him if the knee presents well tomorrow and it's just a knock or, obviously, it's very early to tell if there's something more than a knock," Iraola explained. Despite losing Munoz before the interval, Liverpool still produced a clinical display to dispatch Club Brugge. Two goals from Alexander Isak, alongside a strike from Florian Wirtz, sealed the 3-0 triumph and made it four wins in five Champions League matches this season. Munoz faces race for Everton clash Attention now turns swiftly to Thursday's assessment as the Reds await clarity on whether Munoz has avoided a lengthy spell on the sidelines. Iraola's side return to Premier League action on Sunday with an away fixture against Everton. Whether the £34.5 million winger recovers in time to feature this weekend remains to be seen.

title: Andoni Iraola provides Liverpool injury update after Club Brugge win
summary: Víctor Muñoz Injury Update After Liverpool Beat Club Brugge 3-0Liverpool came away from Belgium with a 3-0 win over Club Brugge, but the main talking point was Victor Munoz and the knee injury that ...
content: Andoni Iraola provides Liverpool injury update after Club Brugge win Víctor Muñoz Injury Update After Liverpool Beat Club Brugge 3-0 Liverpool came away from Belgium with a 3-0 win over Club Brugge, but the main talking point was Victor Munoz and the knee injury that forced the youngster off before half-time. Munoz went into an aggressive challenge with Jorne Spileers and came off second best after what looked like a clash of knees. He stayed down in obvious pain, Liverpool’s medical staff were called on, and the delay was long enough to raise concern on the pitch and on the bench. A stretcher was brought out, which usually tells you plenty. In this case, it was not needed. Munoz left the pitch under his own steam, albeit with a heavy limp and clear discomfort. That matters. Players who can walk off are not automatically fine, but it does suggest the situation may be less serious than it first looked. IMAGO Andoni Iraola gives early Victor Munoz verdict Iraola did not overplay it after full-time. He said what he knew and no more. “[Munoz’s injury] is the worst part of the game, definitely,” Iraola said post-match. He added: “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished. “It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock. “But in the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.” Liverpool injury concern before Merseyside derby That is the sensible reading of it. Painful, yes. Serious, not confirmed. Liverpool will assess him properly, and timing is the issue here. The Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium is next, and availability remains uncertain. This is awkward for Liverpool because they were already missing Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch in Bruges. Squad depth helps, but losing another option before a derby is hardly ideal. Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool as Alexander Isak strikes again Before Munoz went off, Liverpool had already taken control. Dominik Szoboszlai supplied Alexander Isak for the opener after 13 minutes, with the striker finishing from close range. Florian Wirtz made it 2-0, and Isak added his second to complete a straightforward 3-0 win. The result was comfortable. The Munoz injury was not. For now, Iraola’s post-match comments offer Liverpool some encouragement.

title: Andoni Iraola provides Victor Munoz injury update after Liverpool’s win at Club Brugge
summary: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored the goals as the Reds eased past Club Brugge 3-0 in Belgium
content: Andoni Iraola has provided an update on Victor Munoz after the winger was forced off injured in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge . The only downside on a night the Reds they kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League this season, Munoz took a heavy blow to the knee and was replaced by Rio Ngumoha in the 42nd minute. The Spaniard, who scored his third Premier League goal in the routing of Manchester United on the weekend, was in visible agony as he was being treated but Iraola has revealed that the pain had subsided by the end of the match. “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” said Iraola. Liverpool’s Victor Munoz (right) leaves the pitch (Bruno Fahy/PA) “It has been a knock on the knee so now we have to see how it presents tomorrow and see if it is just a knock – but it is very early to tell if there is something more. “In the moment it was very painful and after the game I talked to him and he was more optimistic.” Iraola was nevertheless delighted with his two £100m men Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz as the pair’s goals edged Liverpool closer to Champions League qualification.. Isak scored at either end of the game to take his tally to 10 for the season – on target in his last six away games – with Wirtz continuing his good form with a sixth in five games for club and country. Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the new format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February. “I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” said Iraola. On Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily. “The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations. “In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit. “Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.” Florian Wirtz (left) impressed once again (Virginie Lefour/PA) Isak said he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”. He added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.” Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish. “Both are now in a good place,” he said. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse. “The important part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”

title: Anthony Gordon makes history! Barcelona star smashes RARE Cristiano Ronaldo & Karim Benzema records during Champions League masterclass against Sabah
summary: Anthony Gordon continues to justify his hefty price tag at Barcelona after a historic night in the Champions League saw him eclipse a long-standing record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. The England international was the catalyst for a dominant Blaugrana display in Azerbaijan, proving exactly why the Catalan giants moved so decisively for his signature last summer.
content: Anthony Gordon continues to justify his hefty price tag at Barcelona after a historic night in the Champions League saw him eclipse a long-standing record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. The England international was the catalyst for a dominant Blaugrana display in Azerbaijan, proving exactly why the Catalan giants moved so decisively for his signature last summer. Gordon inspires dominant Barcelona victory in Baku Gordon delivered a Man of the Match display on Wednesday night as Barcelona cruised to a 4-1 Champions League triumph over Sabah at the Baku Olympic Stadium. The England winger struck twice in Azerbaijan to spearhead another commanding European victory for the Catalan side. His latest brace continued an impressive debut campaign in Spain following his £69m transfer in May. Having arrived amid initial scepticism, Gordon now boasts five goals and five assists across all competitions, rapidly establishing himself as a standout summer acquisition. Shattering Ronaldo and Benzema's Champions League records Finding the net twice against Sabah saw Gordon become the first player in Champions League history to score six away goals in a single country within one calendar year. That tally eclipses the previous benchmark of five shared by former Real Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo, who achieved the feat in Turkey in 2013, and Karim Benzema, who matched it in England in 2022. The double also handed Gordon the all-time Champions League record for the most away goals scored by an English player in one nation. His latest strikes in Azerbaijan added to the four goals he registered in the country for Newcastle against Qarabag during last season's competition. Relentless attacking mindset fuels Baku love affair Gordon's clinical edge in Baku underlined the aggressive philosophy driving Barcelona's European campaign, with the attacker insisting the visitors refused to ease off even after taking control of the tie. Speaking after the final whistle, he said: "Even when we were 3-0 up, we didn't stop attacking. We kept trying to score. That's our style, and I think it's very important." Despite walking away with the Man of the Match trophy and a pair of historic records, the former Newcastle forward admitted he left the pitch slightly frustrated at missing out on a treble. He added: " Baku must be a very special place for me ... I should have scored another hat-trick tonight, but I wasted that chance with my left foot." Deportivo trip and Manchester City clash await Barcelona now turn their attention to an away trip to Deportivo this weekend, where Gordon will aim to build on his tally this term. Maintaining that sharp attacking rhythm will be vital as the Catalan side look to carry their momentum forward. European action then resumes on December 8, when Barcelona host Manchester City at Camp Nou. With Gordon in record-breaking form on the continental stage, the fixture offers another major test for the summer signing.

title: Arsenal has doubts over giving key man a new contract

content: Arsenal has doubts over giving key man a new contract Arsenal have been offering new contracts to several members of their first team in recent weeks, and more players are expected to receive improved deals at the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners have enjoyed considerable success on the pitch in recent seasons, rewarding the efforts of a squad that has worked hard to maintain high standards. Much of that progress has come under Mikel Arteta, whose players have continued to work towards making the team competitive. The club want to maintain that progress, and securing the futures of key members of the squad remains part of their plans. However, not every contract situation is straightforward. There is one player Arteta would reportedly like to see commit his future to Arsenal, but there are concerns within the club about whether to offer him a new deal. Arsenal have doubts over Odegaard’s next contract That player is Martin Odegaard, although Football Insider reports that there are doubts at board level about the prospect of handing him a new contract. Arsenal are reportedly concerned that the midfielder may not develop much further and could begin to decline, with the feeling that he is no longer performing at the highest level of his game. Those concerns appear to have influenced the club’s thinking, despite Odegaard remaining a regular member of the team. The situation creates a difference between Arteta’s reported preference and the board’s position. While the manager would like to secure the midfielder’s future, the decision-makers at the club are understood to be more cautious about committing to another deal. Martin Odegaard v Brentford. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Gunners assess Odegaard’s long-term future Odegaard has remained involved in the first team, but Arsenal do not currently view his performances in the same way as those of some of their other players. The club reportedly have doubts about whether he can continue to improve and maintain the level expected of him. That does not mean Arsenal are necessarily preparing for his departure. Rather, the concern is whether offering him a new contract would be the right decision for the club at this stage. The Gunners have been rewarding several players for their contributions , but Odegaard’s situation appears to be different. title: Barcelona duo make strong case for bigger role under Flick after impressive performance vs Sabah
summary: Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah was not a routine win for Hansi Flick.This is because the likes of Alejandro Balde and Karim Adeyemi delivered performances that strengthened thei...
content: Barcelona duo make strong case for bigger role under Flick after impressive performance vs Sabah Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah was not a routine win for Hansi Flick. This is because the likes of Alejandro Balde and Karim Adeyemi delivered performances that strengthened their claims for greater involvement, showing the German manager that his squad possesses valuable alternatives during a demanding run of fixtures. With Lamine Yamal unavailable and Raphinha starting on the bench, Flick made several changes to his starting line-up in Azerbaijan. As such, Balde, Adeyemi, Gavi, Jules Kounde and Gabriel Jesus were among those given opportunities to impress, and two players in particular made the most of their minutes. Adeyemi delivers in Lamine Yamal’s absence Adeyemi was one of Barcelona’s most influential attacking players , combining direct running with effective pressing and movement. Karim Adeyemi was unstoppable against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Selected to occupy the position usually associated with Yamal, the German winger showed that Barcelona can maintain their attacking threat without relying exclusively on their teenage star. Apart from the brilliant goal he scored from Balde’s cross, Adeyemi also helped initiate the move for Anthony Gordon’s opener, provided the assist for Barcelona’s second and then finished the third himself, which strengthens his case for a more prominent role under Flick. Balde brings attacking quality back to Barcelona Furthermore, Balde also used the opportunity to show why he remains an important option on the left flank. After limited playing time earlier in the season, the defender brought greater energy and attacking intent to Barcelona’s build-up. His intelligent forward passes helped create opportunities for Gordon, while his outstanding low delivery for Adeyemi’s goal showed the quality he can provide in the final third. Alejandro Balde delivered an assist for Karim Adeyemi’s goal. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) The injury that forced Balde off was an unfortunate setback, particularly after such an encouraging performance. Barcelona will now need to assess his condition before determining when he can return. Flick gains valuable options before demanding fixtures Barcelona’s slow start against Sabah was indeed a concern, with the home side hitting the post before the visitors established control. However, the attacking contributions of Adeyemi and Balde, among others, helped Flick’s team recover. The result also improved Barcelona’s goal difference in the Champions League, which will be an important consideration in the league phase. Now, with Manchester City, Como and Sporting CP approaching in the Champions League next, Flick will need contributions from across his squad, and it is encouraging to see Adeyemi and Balde have provided compelling evidence that they deserve more opportunities.

Because Pérez refused to withdraw his remarks, Barcelona “will continue to defend its interests,” said club president Joan Laporta. Pérez said the case is an “unprecedented case of corruption” and the “biggest scandal in history.” A report from The Athletic mentions that Barcelona will also file a case against Florentino Pérez because of those quotes. “We consider we have to defend Barça’s interests when barbarities like that are said around, and especially coming from the biggest representative of another football club. I saw that in Madrid’s general assembly they kept talking about Barça in the same terms. They are obsessed with talking about Barça. In the end we will end up asking them for royalties, because they are boosting their image thanks to Barça,” said Laporta.

content: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report Barcelona extended their winning run to five matches in all competitions following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League. Apart from the stellar attacking display, a key highlight of the night was the debut of La Masia starlet Alex Campos. The young defender came in as a 64th minute replacement for Frenkie de Jong and had a solid enough outing. An answer to Barcelona’s defensive problems? Alex Campos made his debut against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) It is no secret that Barcelona are struggling defensively. Even Hansi Flick looked visibly frustrated after the team conceded a goal against Sabah. The team simply lacks enough depth in central defence. But as reported by Diario SPORT , Flick may have found his answer in the form of Campos. With Andreas Christensen still struggling with injuries, Pau Cubarsi carrying a knock and the likes of Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde often required elsewhere, Barcelona have been crying out for a reliable centre-back. De Jong has done well to chip in, but he is not a natural in this position, leaving Flick with Gerard Martin as the only other option. Campos’ cameo in Baku may prove to be a first step towards him becoming a real alternative for Barcelona. The report frames the youngster as a potential example of Barcleona solving the defensive problem from within. The Catalans have a solid track record of doing so, having previously solved multiple problems for giving chances to academy players such as Marc Casado, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Cubarsi himself. What does Campos bring to the table? Campos is rated highly by Bojan. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As far as his profile is concerned, Campos is quite similar to Cubarsi. Originally a midfielder before Barcelona converted him into a central defender, Campos’ natural qualities include playing out from the back and the ability to join attacks. He is also a genuine threat from set-pieces and is very efficient on the ball. Under Juliano Belletti, however, his defensive game has improved enormously and he is now regarded as a solid, reliable operator in central defence. Campos is also quite versatile, as he can perform both as a left and a right sided centre-back. He is comfortable filling in as a holding midfielder as well. Perhaps more importantly, Campos rarely loses his composure. He is already held in high regard by the likes of Bojan Krkic and Belletti and it will be interesting to see if he is used more often by Flick in the coming weeks.

title: Bayern Munich handed Michael Olise injury boost

content: Bayern Munich handed Michael Olise injury boost Bayern Munich have received a welcome boost on the injury front, with Bild reporting that Michael Olise has resumed running training. The Frenchman suffered a bruised foot in Friday's 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln and subsequently missed Wednesday's 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League. With Bayern dealing with several injury problems in attack, the German champions will be hoping to welcome the influential winger back as soon as possible. However, it's currently unclear if Olise will be fit in time for Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Hamburger SV. In addition to Olise, Manuel Neuer, Alphonso Davies, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari also missed Wednesday's game. Neuer, Kane and Saibari are all set to remain sidelined long term.

title: 'Blackburn turning performances into points'

title: Bolton Wanderers 1-3 West Bromwich Albion - fans' verdict
summary: Here are your thoughts after West Bromwich Albion won 3-1 at Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship.
content: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after West Bromwich Albion won 3-1 at Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Trotters fans Andrew: We are going to struggle but we are always there, so no need to panic just yet. David : Lack of class at this level plus individual errors and naivety are killing us. We need to learn quickly or it's going to be a long winter. Jordan : Bolton are far too passive, sitting deep and waiting to be punished. It's starting to feel like the manager isn't capable of getting the best out of our team. Poor decisions almost every game around the starting 11 means we're almost always having to chase a game, especially at home, leaving us wide open to attack and getting punished further. We have a decent squad but need to use it better. Albion fans Nathan : Football is a funny old game at times, I thought we dominated the first half, although we only had one goal to show for all the possession. The second half Bolton were a lot better and I was worried that they were more likely to score a winner. Good teams always find a way to win so I'm glad we were able to!

title: Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City - fans' verdict
summary: Here are your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship.
content: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to make it an EFL record 24 home games without a win for the Clarets while Blues closed the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Clarets fans Lynne: Tragic. No desire to push forward or take responsibility in front of goal. The fans are despondent as are the players. It's so sad to watch. Brian : The worst performance ever. Many will not renew season tickets until Pace has gone. Steve : Going backwards. Losing possession has been a problem all season, as has schoolboy defending. We are so so slow building attacks it's ridiculous. It's like we allow any team to get back in shape before we attack. Kyle Walker has been terrible and even Amdouni, who has been loved by the fans, has had stinkers in the last two games. I can see us going down again and the owners have created all this. They should resign as a board and sell up and go back to the US. Darren : Woeful, no fight in any of them. We are staring at League One football without a doubt. Mark : We were shocking. Our defence is about as useful as a chocolate fireguard. Vardy should have started, he'd have gotten on the end of Ramazani's crosses and balls into the box. It was a very lacklustre performance. On these performances we're down. Blues fans Phil : A routine win against a very poor team. In Blues' favour it's not the easiest place to visit on a cold winter evening. Gary : Good start but some sloppy play meant we needed Beadle to be on top form. Fry and Neumann excellent, Klarer has a rival for his place now, some puzzling substitutions from Davies. David : It's wins like this that win Championships and promotions. They build confidence which is so important. Daniel : Very professional performance, could have been more comfortable. Burnley had very good possession but no end product. Looking forward to upcoming games, real battle at the top now, bring it on. John : This win looks good but we could easily have lost if Burnley had taken their chances. In my opinion we were quite lucky in some ways.

title: "There are certainly options" – Eberl keeps door open to January transfers at Bayern
summary: Bayern Munich's injury problems came into sharp focus on Wednesday as a depleted side suffered a 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League, bringing their unbeaten start to the season to an end...
content: "There are certainly options" – Eberl keeps door open to January transfers at Bayern Bayern Munich's injury problems came into sharp focus on Wednesday as a depleted side suffered a 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League, bringing their unbeaten start to the season to an end. With key players such as Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Alphonso Davies sidelined, the defeat only added to the growing speculation over whether Bayern might strengthen their squad in January. Speaking to DAZN after the game, board member for sport Max Eberl left the door open to new signings, while stressing that any potential arrival would have to be a “perfect fit”. "We'll take a look at it. First and foremost, what's important is what the squad looks like in January," Eberl said. He stressed that the club will not “rush into anything” and instead assess the situation calmly. "There are certainly options, but whatever we do would have to be a perfect fit," Eberl added. Speaking before the game, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund pointed out that, with several players, including Michael Olise and Alphonso Davies, expected to return in a not too distant future, there's currently no intention to make any additions to the squad in January. "That's why making signings isn't our plan at the moment. We hope the situation will look different again soon and that we can collect plenty of points with the players we already have," Freund said.

title: Champions League power rankings: Real Madrid surge – while rivals hit by injuries
summary: Real Madrid remain the lone team with an 100 per cent record, while only PSG and Arsenal are now also unbeaten after a shock loss for Bayern Munich
content: Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season. The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich ’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below. ↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona, 6-0 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Roma Fixtures: Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h) Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL issues. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Dembele will be without Kvaratskhelia and Doue for the rest of the season (Reuters) ↔️ 2. Barcelona Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG, 3-0 v Aston Villa, 4-1 v Sabah Fixtures: Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h) Even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the big question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove. Gordon scored twice for Barcelona against Sabah (Reuters) ↔️ 3. Arsenal Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille, 2-2 v Bayern Munich, 2-1 v Slavia Prague, 1-1 v Borussia Dortmund Fixtures: Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h) The arrival of winter is perhaps leading to some frustration, particularly in front of goal . Arsenal remain unbeaten but they were punished for not taking their opportunities as they dropped points at home to Borussia Dortmund, a result which means their place in the top-eight is not assured yet ahead of tough games against Real Madrid and Real Betis. Viktor Gyokeres was on target against Dortmund but Arsenal dropped points (Getty) ⬆️🟢 4. Real Madrid (+2 from 6) Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma, 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 3-2 v AEK Athens, 5-1 v PSV Fixtures: Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a) Real Madrid have come into a remarkable run of form, with a thumping win over PSV making it 10 wins in a row in all competitions under Jose Mourinho. It’s funny, in the Champions League, Real Madrid have trailed several games yet have maximum points. Now, the 15-time Champions League winners are not just managing to find a way, but they are blowing teams off the park. Jude Bellingham scored a brilliant volley in their big win over PSV (Getty) ⬆️🟢 5. Liverpool (+2 from 7) Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-3 v Fenerbahce, 3-0 Club Brugge Fixtures: Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h) Before Andoni Iraola’s first season, it felt like so much depended on the potential of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz coming good in the Liverpool attack. Well, the signs of the past few weeks have been hugely promising as Isak and Wirtz continued to build their partnership in the 3-0 win at Club Brugge, with the Reds bouncing back from their shock defeat at Fenerbahce last time out. Florian Wirtz got on the scoresheet again in Belgium (Getty) ⬇️🔴 6. Bayern Munich (-2 from 4) Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal, 2-0 v Atletico Madrid, 1-2 v Lille Fixtures: Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h) The major concern for the German champions is the fitness of their Ballon d’Or holder Harry Kane, who will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury. Bayern have plenty of games to play until then and the question is whether they can get through to the top eight without Kane to avoid an additional play-off round. A stunning 2-1 defeat at Lille, which featured some calamitous defending and a truly remarkable Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal (honestly, go and check it out ...), saw Bayern drop to 15th in the table. Kane will be out until the knockout stages of the Champions League (Getty) ⬇️🔴 7. Man City (-2 from 5) Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG, 5-1 v AEK Athens, 3-2 v Leipzig, 2-2 v Napoli Fixtures: Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a) Three defeats from four in the Premier League have well and truly taken shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well . After another sloppy performance against Napoli and the returning Kevin De Bruyne means it is now 10 games in a row without a clean sheet. City now face a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona and likely require a result to avoid dropping out of the top eight. Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli (PA) ⬆️🟢 8. Como (+2 from 10) Results: 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 2-3 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Manchester United, 9-1 v Lens, 1-0 v AEK Athens Fixtures: Real Betis (a), Paris Saint Germain (h), Barcelona (a) Up at the top of the table with the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Barcelona, the Champions League debutants are certainly making a name for themselves. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side didn’t quite hit the same heights against AEK Athens after their nine-goal dismantling of poor Lens, but look what comes next. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase, after a tricky trip to Real Betis, are going to be fascinating. Inter Milan Results: 1-2 v Real Madrid, 3-4 v Club Brugge, 1-0 v Shakhtar, 3-0 v Feyenoord, 2-0 v Stuttgart Fixtures: Borussia Dortmund (a), Liverpool (h), Slovan Bratislava (a) After starting with back-to-back defeats, Inter have responded with three consecutive wins. There was more good news in the 2-0 win over Stuttgart as Lautaro Martinez marked his return from injury after a month on the sidelines with a goal. Lautaro Martinez celebrated his return from injury (Getty) ⬆️🟢 10. Sure, they’ve got five points from five games in the Champions League and sit outside the top 24 in the league table. But a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain continued Roma’s impressive season under Gian Piero Gasperini; they remain unbeaten in Serie A and now have a more favourable run of games in the Champions League. On performances alone, they’ve earned a place in our top 10. Donyell Malen scored Roma’s equaliser in Paris (Reuters) ↔️ 11 . Atletico Madrid ↔️ 12. Borussia Dortmund ↔️ 13. Real Betis ⬇️ 🔴 14. title: Chelsea forward wanted by European giants
summary: Chelsea Hold Firm on Estêvão as PSG Weigh January Transfer Window MoveChelsea are understood to have no intention of letting Estêvão leave, despite fresh interest from Paris Saint-Germain ahead of...
content: Chelsea forward wanted by European giants Chelsea Hold Firm on Estêvão as PSG Weigh January Transfer Window Move Chelsea are understood to have no intention of letting Estêvão leave, despite fresh interest from Paris Saint-Germain ahead of the January transfer window. The latest reports suggest the European champions are reviewing attacking targets after a damaging injury setback, with Estêvão now firmly in the frame. According to Caught Offside, PSG are assessing their options after Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both suffered serious knee injuries. That situation has forced a rethink in Paris, and Chelsea’s young Brazilian has emerged as one of the names under consideration. Photo IMAGO PSG interest puts Estêvão in focus The report states that “PSG have included Estêvão on their shortlist alongside Bayern Munich winger Luis Díaz and RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa.” It also adds that “Luis Enrique is reluctant to rush into the transfer market and wants to assess his existing attacking options before making a final decision.” Even so, there appears to have been early contact. Another key line in the report says PSG “contacted Chelsea regarding Estêvão’s availability, only for the west London club to quickly dismiss the possibility of a deal.” That is a significant detail. It indicates Chelsea’s position is clear, at least for now, and there is no appetite at Stamford Bridge to entertain offers. Chelsea stance on Estêvão reflects long-term plan This feels like a straightforward situation in one sense. Chelsea rate the player highly, PSG admire him, and the selling club are resisting. Estêvão is still only 19, and while “his opportunities to play regular football have been limited”, there is evidently a belief internally that his pathway should remain in west London. The reasoning is easy to follow. Chelsea invested in him because of his ceiling, and the source makes that case strongly, describing his “enormous potential, exceptional dribbling ability and creativity in the final third”. Those are attributes clubs at the top of the European game monitor very closely, especially when the player is already attracting this level of attention. Regular minutes now look crucial for Chelsea winger There is also a wider point here for Chelsea. It is one thing to reject interest, it is another to create the right conditions for development. The report argues that “Selling Estêvão at this stage of his career would be incredibly short-sighted,” and it is difficult to disagree. It goes further, adding that “Giving the Brazilian greater responsibility and consistent playing time could prove far more rewarding than any substantial transfer offer from Paris.” That may be the central issue in the months ahead. Chelsea are right to protect a major talent, but PSG’s move is a reminder that elite clubs are watching closely. If Estêvão is part of the future, Chelsea now need to show it with meaningful opportunities. Our View This is the kind of report that immediately creates anxiety because it touches a nerve. Chelsea have collected elite young talent for years, but there has to be a point where potential turns into trust. If PSG are already looking at Estêvão this seriously, then everybody in football can see what Chelsea have on their hands. The fear is whether Chelsea will handle him properly. Rejecting an approach is the easy part. The hard part is giving him a genuine route into the side, especially when attacking selections can become crowded and short-term pressure often drives decisions. If he stays on the margins, this story will not go away. It will grow. Other clubs will keep asking the same question, and sooner or later the player may ask it too. There is also a nagging concern that Chelsea sometimes speak like a club building for the future while acting like a club chasing immediate fixes. Estêvão should not become another case of waiting, watching and wondering when his moment will come. If he is as special as this report suggests, then he needs proper minutes, proper responsibility and proper backing. Watching a talent of this level become a star somewhere else after being stockpiled would be maddening. Chelsea cannot afford to treat him as a luxury asset. He has to be developed with conviction. Otherwise, interest from PSG today could become a real problem tomorrow. Source: Caught Offside
