title: 'He's lost a little bit of confidence' - Peter Schmeichel highlights 'sad truth' behind Senne Lammens' Man Utd struggles after Sporting errors
summary: Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel has offered a blunt assessment of Senne Lammens' current form following a difficult night for the goalkeeper in the Champions League. While the 24-year-old showcased his shot-stopping ability with a penalty save, a series of costly errors allowed Sporting to fight back and claim a 2-2 draw in Lisbon.
content: Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel has offered a blunt assessment of Senne Lammens' current form following a difficult night for the goalkeeper in the Champions League. While the 24-year-old showcased his shot-stopping ability with a penalty save, a series of costly errors allowed Sporting to fight back and claim a 2-2 draw in Lisbon. Costly errors overshadow Lammens' penalty heroics Lammens endured a difficult European outing against Sporting as two unforced errors undermined a promising start. After denying Colombian forward Luis Suarez from the penalty spot in the first half, the Belgian keeper quickly conceded a foul in the box, allowing Suarez to convert. Matters worsened after the break when Lammens spilled a high delivery into the area. Suarez reacted quickest, finishing acrobatically to earn the Portuguese side a point. Schmeichel points to World Cup hangover and defensive failings Speaking to CBS Sports , former United keeper Schmeichel declined to say if Lammens should be dropped, suggesting new boss Mauricio Pochettino's staff could spark a turnaround. "I don’t know [at what point should Man Utd drop him]," Schmeichel said. "Mauricio Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him." Schmeichel traced the 24-year-old's dip back to Belgium's tournament exit against Spain. He added: "I don’t know if you remember in the World Cup, he came against Spain and made a bit of a mistake, [Mikel] Merino scored and they [Belgium] got knocked out, and I feel like he’s lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered. "As a goalkeeper when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and the sad truth is that they haven’t been able to do that and of course, that makes it so much worse. I like him a lot but today was not a great day for him." Fernandes demands collective accountability Lammens' shaky start to the term contrasts sharply with his encouraging debut campaign at United following an £18.1 million transfer from Royal Antwerp. Despite his costly lapses in Portugal, club captain Bruno Fernandes defended his team-mate and demanded shared accountability across the squad. "It’s part of football, mistakes are part of football, and from that, you get goals," Fernandes said. "But, obviously, it’s not an individual sport, so everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and everything we do bad. "I think the main thing and the most important thing is to understand we need to be together, in the good and in the bad moments, and it’s not going to change the belief we have in each other." Pressure mounts on Lammens as Darlow waits in the wings With his confidence dented, Lammens faces a stern test to rediscover his debut-season form under Pochettino's new goalkeeping coach. Summer signing Karl Darlow remains waiting in the wings if a change is required, with the former Newcastle and Leeds United keeper yet to make a Premier League appearance this season.

title: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare
summary: Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment.However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half o...
content: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment. However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half of their game against PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League. The defensive duo of Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao looked completely out of sorts , prompting Jose Mourinho to make changes in the second half. Mourinho identifies a key issue Mourinho wants more quality from his second squad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho believes that his rotation options are simply not performing as expected. The Real Madrid coach has observed that when the fringe players come in, Real Madrid often lose their brightness and competitive edge. It is a pattern that Mourinho has noticed on multiple occasions, with the likes of Rudiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Alvaro Carreras and Eduardo Camavinga often failing to perform to the expected level. These players have lacked the quality and the consistency the first-choice XI has provided this season, and the 5-1 win over PSV was the latest example. Mourinho made six changes to the starting lineup, but the team struggled in the first half and conceded. He had experienced similar situations in the comebacks against Celta Vigo and AEK Athens. A necessary balancing act Mourinho is using Luis Enrique’s playbook. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Despite this shortcoming from lesser-used players, Mourinho remains committed to using the full depth of his squad. The Portuguese is working on managing a demanding schedule in December through a selection rest plan. He is determined to keep his first-choice players fresh for key matches. With Real Madrid facing a relentless run of fixtures, rotation will indeed play a key role in the month of December, and that is when Mourinho needs his second-fiddle stars to perform well. In many ways, Mourinho is applying the same roadmap used by Luis Enrique at PSG, protecting his important players in selected games. He rested Arda Guler and Tchouameni against AEK, and left Jude Bellingham on the bench against PSV Eindhoven. This is yet another indicator that Mourinho has stressed massively on ensuring the well-being of his trusted individuals. But for this formula to work, players such as Trent, Rudiger, Camavinga, and others must step up their game.

title: Joshua Kimmich slams club's 'not Bayern-like' treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala
summary: LILLE, France (AP) — Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.
content: LILLE, France (AP) — Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures. Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO. Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image. “What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public,” Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. “It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either.” Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition. “It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself,” Kimmich added. Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension. Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension. “This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared,” Bayern said. Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue. Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern has lost the lead in the Bundesliga and slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings. ___ See AP’s full soccer coverage here

title: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter
summary: Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP.ControversyPochettino was denied his first win as United...
content: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Controversy Pochettino was denied his first win as United head coach, with multiple bizarre refereeing decisions going against him and his players. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled out an Amad Diallo goal during the second half, having adjudged Youri Tielemans to have committed a foul in the build-up. Marciniak’s whistle came just before Amad found the net, ruling out any VAR intervention. The Polish referee compounded matters by awarding Sporting a debatable first-half penalty and disallowing what would have been a late United winner for a push on goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The decision to chalk off United’s goal seemed baffling given that he allowed a similar Suárez goal to stand when there was slight contact with Senne Lammens . Pochettino hit out at the decisions in his post-match remarks to reporters , but he chose to emphasise the positives and the fine attitude his players displayed. In an interview with MUTV , Zirkzee acknowledged how costly the referee’s shocking performance had been, but insisted it was solely down to him and his teammates to deliver the victory. Zirkzee’s verdict The Dutchman told club media, “In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us. We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.” “But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.” He continued, “Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take.” “But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move onto the next game.” Zirkzee said of his return to the starting XI, “I’m very happy; every game you play for this club is an honour. I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.” “For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible. All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.” Looking ahead to Saturday’s meeting with Brentford, Zirkzee remarked, “It’s a big test. The fans deserve a result and all we want is a result. We’ve got to dig ourselves out of the trenches.” United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table heading into the game against Brentford.

title: Joshua Zirkzee reveals Manchester United dressing room reaction to Senne Lammens howlers in Sporting draw
summary: Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee has opened up on the atmosphere inside the dressing room following Senne Lammens' difficult night in the Champions League. The Belgian goalkeeper suffered a personal nightmare in Lisbon, committing two high-profile errors that ultimately saw victory slip away against Sporting.
content: Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee has opened up on the atmosphere inside the dressing room following Senne Lammens' difficult night in the Champions League. The Belgian goalkeeper suffered a personal nightmare in Lisbon, committing two high-profile errors that ultimately saw victory slip away against Sporting. Costly errors and VAR drama deny Pochettino first win Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first victory as Manchester United manager following a chaotic 2-2 draw with Sporting at the Jose Alvalade. Bruno Fernandes fired the visitors into a 2-1 lead with a quickfire double early in the second half, after Lammens had saved a penalty only to rush off his line 75 seconds later and concede a second spot-kick converted by Luis Suarez. The Colombian striker later capitalised when Lammens spilled a cross at his feet with 10 minutes remaining to snatch an equaliser. United were also left fuming at Polish referee Szymon Marciniak, who blew for a free-kick just before Amad scored prior to half-time and later saw a late winner chalked off after VAR judged Patrick Dorgu had fouled the goalkeeper. Zirkzee insists Man Utd squad are backing Lammens Despite the gaffes continuing Lammens' uncertain second season in Manchester , Zirkzee revealed his team-mates chose to give the goalkeeper breathing room in the dressing room while backing his strong mentality. "In this moment, we just give him space," said Zirkzee. "Not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne’s a great kid. He's got a good head on him. "And we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. And we didn't draw because of him. I'm also someone who likes to look at myself and I didn't score." Asked how important it was to show support to Lammens, the forward added: "It's everything. This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves. Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper." Officiating frustration and an 'us against the world' mindset Controversial refereeing has now marred both of Pochettino's opening matches in charge, following Leny Yoro's wrongful eighth-minute red card at Anfield . That growing sense of injustice has fuelled a siege mentality inside the camp, though Zirkzee refused to blame the officials entirely. "Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick," he said. "But as I said, we've got a locker room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. And if it's us against the world, so be it. "For the team that we are, we shouldn't really be looking at what the referee decides, but you cannot deny that it was some key decisions that weren't in our favour, to put it like that. "But, as I said, we shouldn't really be looking at the referee. All we have to do is look at ourselves. In the end, I think we lost because of small details, little mistakes. But we definitely have something to build on, mainly the way we started the second half. I think that's something we can build on and move on with." Brentford clash offers immediate chance to respond United now return to Premier League action against Brentford, where Pochettino will again seek his maiden victory at the helm. Cutting out costly lapses in concentration remains the immediate challenge if the squad are to turn improved displays into three points. Replicating the intensity that produced Fernandes' double after the interval in Lisbon will be vital as United look to steady their campaign and put back-to-back frustrations behind them.

title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
summary: Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers.
content: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. What's next for MLS play-offs? For now, clubs must navigate the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs under the existing system before the overhaul arrives alongside the league's new competition calendar in 2027-28. Some finer details of the revamped format still require clarification. It remains unknown how hosting order for the two-legged ties will be assigned, although the last MLS format to use home-and-away series gave the higher seed home advantage for the decisive second leg.

title: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish?
summary: Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended ...
content: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish? Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match. That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February. Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust How many more points do Liverpool need for top-eight finish? At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game. That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home). The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare. That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton. Top-eight finish well within reach for Liverpool With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced. The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens. That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

title: Midweek Warm-up: What a week for Bayern Munich, huh?; Don’t meet your heroes; Champions League predictions; and MORE!
summary: It’s a Champions League showdown for Bayern Munich
content: Photo: Peter Kneffel/dpa (Photo by Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Images) “What a week, huh?” “Captain, it’s Wednesday.” Bayern Munich could probably use that exchange as the unofficial motto for the last several d ays. Between the public discussion surrounding J amal Musiala, comments from club leadership, questions about his contract, and now reporting from Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (via @iMiaSan Mia ) about Vincent Kompany reassuring players and club employees regarding Musia la’s health, it has been an exhausting news cycle. According to Falk and Agardi, Kompany told his players during a dressing-room team talk that they should have absolutely no concerns about Musiala or his health, assuring them that their teammate is in excellent health and full of energy. Kompany reportedly delivered the same reassurance to several other club employees. The reassurance comes after a week in which Musiala has seemingly become the center of a wider Bayern Munich debate that has extended well beyond football. Comments and crit icism from Jan-Christian Dreesen, Uli Hoeneß, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge regarding Musiala, his contract, and his situation have helped fuel the perception of a growing divide between the player a nd the club. What might ordinarily be an internal conversation about a player’s development, recovery, contractual future, and expectations has increasingly played out publicly, leaving Musiala at the center of a debate that is difficult to separate from the footballing realities. That is where this entire situation has become particularly uncomfortable. Musiala is not just a contract negotiat ion, a talking point for club executives, or a headline generator. He is a player recovering, trying to get back to his best, and one whose importance to Bayern Munich is difficult to oversta te. Public discourse can easily turn a complicated situation into a perceived confrontation, but that does not necessarily reflect what is happening behind closed doors. Ultimately, though, thi s is about Jamal Musiala’s health. The hope should be that he gets fully healthy, regains his confidence, and returns to the form that made him one of the mo st highly regarded talents in world football. That is what matters most, regardless of the noise, the speculation, or the conversations about who knew what and when. Will he get back to a top level? Is he worth the massive contract? Should Bayern Munich seek to renegotiate? For now, it is probably time to put th is ordeal aside, take a breath, and focus on what Bayern Munich actually has in front of it — a Champions League game. The rest can wait. Song of the Midweek: “Young Again” by Shinedown In contrast to our normal fare, here is a newer song. Released earlier this year on EI8HT , this one caught my attention, and it felt like a good little change from a lot of my reminiscing about music from years closer to my prime (hell yeah!). Enjoy: In lieu of an Entertainment Rundown As the podcast listeners know, I’ve been on the road a bit and had no time to watch anything, but there is a topic that needs to be addressed… Manuel Neuer has found himself caught up in yet ano ther controversy, and while the latest discussion surrounding the Bayern Munich captain might change how some people view him personally, it should not change how we evalua te him as a footballer. Those two things can coexist, even if football fandom often struggles to separate them. There is an uncomfortable reality in sports — exceptional athletes are not necessarily exceptional people. Players can make questionable dec isions, display narcissistic tendencies, behave selfishly, or even be genuinely unpleasant individuals, and still be extraordinary at their profession. Football does not automatically mak e someone virtuous, and talent does not require a spotless personal record. Neuer’s legacy as one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation is built on what he has done between the posts, not on whether every decision he has made away from the pitch deserves admiration. Criticism of his conduct is fair, and fans are perfectly enti tled to reassess the person they thought they knew. But that does not erase decades of elite performances. It is another reminder of the old saying, “Do not meet your heroes.” Sometimes the person behind the legend is considerably more complicated than the image we built in our heads. That does not mean the football was any less phenomenal. Predictions When I look in the mirror I can’t believe what I see Tell me, who’s that funky dude Staring back at me? Broken, beaten down, can’t even get around Without an old man cane, I fall and hit the ground Shivering in the cold, I’m bitter and alone Excuse the b*tching I shouldn’t complain I should have no feeling ‘Cause feeling is pain As everything I need is denied me And everything I want is taken away from me But who do I got to blame? Nobody but me Yup, Bayern Munich is, indeed, broken and beaten down and not living “The Good Life” — at least not at this very moment. At some point, though, the squad has to get past t he headlines and conjecture and remember why it is here in the first place: a Champions League tilt vs. LOSC Lille. LOSC Lille is not great, let alone a powerhouse, but it has — at least — had a week not mired in controversy. In addition, while Lille does have some injuries, its front line is mostly intact. The same cannot be said for Bayern Munich, which is limping into the game. At some point, though, the pride wi thin the Bavarians has to show through all of the nonsense going on around the squad. The fight and heart will need to be on full display, and the mentality of a true champion will either be there when the whistle blows or… it won’t. Let’s bank on Bayern Munich remembering exactly who the (expletive removed) it is. title: Milan List Barcelona, Bologna and Frosinone Defenders

content: Milan List Barcelona, Bologna and Frosinone Defenders Milan are shifting their focus from the middle to the left of their defense and are stepping up their efforts to acquire a new specialist in January. They had already been linked to a pair of options before Ruben Amorim stated he was content with his center-backs. According to Calciomercato , the Rossoneri will keep pursuing Noussair Mazraoui , who already worked with their coach, but it’s too early to determine his future, as Manchester United are in a holding pattern after recently hiring Mauricio Pochettino. Milan had also been attached to Gabriele Calvani , who’s showing well at Frosinone for the second consecutive season. He generally plays as a center-back but has some experience wide too. He’s on loan from Genoa, who’s interested in their youngsters Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto. Instead, Alejandro Balde and Juan Miranda are the latest additions to their shortlist. Jorge Mendes has offered the latter to several clubs, as he’s logged just 125 minutes thus far. However, he needs to be convinced to leave Catalunya. Instead, the Bologna man is in the midst of a career season, having already provided six assists. The Felsinei are having trouble with his extension talks and would carefully weigh €15M offers. Our Take on Milan Looking For a Fullback They have to decide whether they want a defensive or an aggressive option, as Amorim has used Mario Gila and Sankhoun Diawara wide whenever everyone was fit in the back to free up their attackers. Instead, other than Calvani, who’s not even left-footed, their rumored targets are all dynamic players. It feels like their search is in its infancy, and the right name hasn’t emerged yet.

title: Pick of the stats: Southampton v Middlesbrough
summary: Here are the key stats for Southampton v Middlesbrough.
content: [BBC] Middlesbrough will aim to extend their lead at the top of the table when they visit Southampton on Friday night (20:00 GMT). The two sides are meeting each other for the first time since Spygate but it will mean more to Boro than a grudge match. A slip up here could see any of the four Midlands teams beneath them steal their place at the apex by the end of the weekend and their automatic promotion spot to boot. It won't be easy though with Saints yet to to lose on home soil this season. Southampton are winless in their last four league games against Middlesbrough (D2 L2) since a 2-1 away win in the Premier League in May 2017. Middlesbrough have gone five away league games without a win at Southampton (D3 L2) since beating them 1-0 in September 2003. Southampton are unbeaten in their last 18 home league games (W14 D4), their best run without losing at St Mary's since going 24 in a row between December 2010 and December 2011. Middlesbrough have failed to score in each of their last two away league games, having 30 shots without success. They haven't gone three Championship away games without a goal since January 2015. ● Cyle Larin has netted 12 goals in 16 home league appearances for Southampton, averaging one every 86 minutes. It's the best ratio by a Saints player to play 500+ minutes across the Premier League, Championship and League One at St Mary's since it opened in 2001. [BBC]

title: 'We play with no fear!' - Mario Hermoso reveals Gian Piero Gasperini's training ground secret after AS Roma halt Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak
summary: Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack.
content: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack. Hermoso inspires fearless Roma to historic Paris point Mario Hermoso set the tone inside five minutes as AS Roma held reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a thrilling 2-2 draw in the first-ever meeting between the clubs on Wednesday night. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. Hermoso, who also went close to adding a second open-play goal, revealed how attacking rotations are rehearsed daily. "With these team-mates who play in attack, we do try to make these moves in training sessions, everyone gets to have a go, and that means us defenders can bring something extra to the team, it's an added benefit," he explained. Addressing the bench impact, Hermoso added: "Everyone in this squad is important, we are set out in a way that we can all be protagonists. Dony, Paulo and Bryan had more minutes in this season, but they came on with the right mentality, and were ready to help get a good result." Building a winning mentality against European champions PSG only breached Roma's open-play organisation through Zabarnyi's 31st-minute corner header and Dembele's 62nd-minute spot-kick after Achraf Hakimi was fouled by Wesley. Hermoso credited Gasperini with transforming Roma's resilience in high-pressure European fixtures. "The coach gives you confidence to believe, to have this mentality of reacting to difficult moments that we suffered not just this season, but over the years," Hermoso told Prime Video . "This is important, given the way the team came in, the way we played this match against a team that has won the last two Champions Leagues. The result is a huge achievement... It's a shame we didn't win, but a point is good." Roma target knockout surge from 25th place Sitting second in Serie A, Roma now turn their focus toward climbing into the Champions League play-off spots from 25th place with five points from five games. "The most important thing is to continue to grow. We want to fight for everything – we have the mentality to do it, we have the quality too. Let's continue like this, with what the coach wants. For us, it's the right path," Hermoso concluded.

title: Pochettino confident Man United will turn things round

title: Real Madrid revive interest in €40m-rated Borussia Dortmund left-back ahead of possible 2027 move – report
summary: Real Madrid have renewed their interest in Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, with the Swedish international still on the club’s scouting radar ahead of the 2027 transfer windows.According...
content: Real Madrid revive interest in €40m-rated Borussia Dortmund left-back ahead of possible 2027 move – report Real Madrid have renewed their interest in Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, with the Swedish international still on the club’s scouting radar ahead of the 2027 transfer windows. According to Bernabeu Digital , the Santiago Bernabeu outfit has continued monitoring Svensson after tracking him for several months last year. In fact, scouts previously travelled to watch the defender during a Champions League match against Atalanta, which helps explain that the interest is not a recent development. Svensson remains on Real Madrid’s shortlist Real Madrid’s interest in Svensson reportedly dates back to last season, when his potential arrival was linked to the possibility of Fran Garcia leaving the club. Daniel Svensson is on Real Madrid’s radar. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) Garcia eventually departed for Real Betis last summer, while Marc Cucurella arrived from Chelsea, and yet Svensson has now re-emerged as a possible option to strengthen the left side of José Mourinho’s defence. Dortmund could demand up to €40 million For what it is worth, the outlet mentions that a potential deal would not be easy to pull off as Svensson is under contract with Borussia Dortmund until 2029, giving the German club a strong negotiating position. As far as his valuation is concerned, some reports have placed Dortmund’s asking price at €35 million to €40 million, while others have suggested a starting figure closer to €30 million. At the same time, the transfer fee alone will not be the only problem for Real Madrid, as Arsenal, Inter Milan and Leeds United have also been linked with the Swedish defender, potentially increasing competition if Madrid decide to pursue him. A possible summer 2027 target Daniel Svensson will not come cheap. (Photo by Pau Barrena/Getty Images) For now, Svensson appears to be in long-term consideration, with a possible move in summer 2027 dependent on Real Madrid’s squad needs and the development of their left-back situation. Speaking of left-backs, Jose Mourinho currently has three options available for that position, namely Cucurella, Alvaro Carreras and Ferland Mendy. This means Real Madrid cannot simply look for a new player for the same role without making necessary space, with Mendy being the most likely candidate to leave next summer. Even so, having options like Cucurella and Carreras will not lower Real Madrid’s negotiation power with the Dortmund defender.

title: Stats: Barcelona superstar Frenkie de Jong achieves remarkable passing milestone against Sabah
summary: Frenkie de Jong produced a remarkable passing performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah, completing all 69 of his attempted passes during a 64-minute appearance. Hansi Flic...
content: Stats: Barcelona superstar Frenkie de Jong achieves remarkable passing milestone against Sabah Frenkie de Jong produced a remarkable passing performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah, completing all 69 of his attempted passes during a 64-minute appearance. Hansi Flick once again deployed the Dutch midfielder at centre-back, using his composure and distribution to help Barcelona control proceedings in Azerbaijan. With defensive absences forcing Flick to explore alternative solutions, De Jong’s performance showed the tactical value of having a midfielder capable of organising possession from deep. Crucially, his display against Sabah followed a similar assignment in Barcelona’s 3-2 league victory over Villarreal . De Jong provides defensive security and exceptional accuracy De Jong had relatively little defensive work against Sabah, whose attacking approach lacked the directness to consistently trouble Barcelona’s back line. He recorded three defensive actions, made a clearance and produced an important interception during a counterattack down the left. Alongside Gerard Martin, the Dutchman remained alert whenever Barcelona needed to defend, but his greatest influence came through his distribution. Statistically, on that note, De Jong has completed 232 of his 236 passes across his last three appearances while playing in defence against Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and Sabah, recording a remarkable 98.3% success rate. Against Sabah, he was perfect, completing 51 of 51 passes in his own half and 18 of 18 in the opposition half. Barcelona midfielder achieves Champions League passing milestone Notably, the 69 successful passes he achieved is now the fifth-highest total by a Barcelona player in a single Champions League match without a misplaced pass since at least the 2003-04 season. For what it is worth, De Jong’s performance was particularly impressive given the responsibility of playing in defence and not in his usual midfield position. His ability to receive possession under pressure and distribute accurately allowed Barcelona to maintain their rhythm and prevent Sabah from gaining sustained momentum. Frenkie de Jong had 100% passing accuracy vs Sabah. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Ultimately, De Jong was substituted in the 64th minute, allowing Barça Atlètic defender Alex Campos to make his first-team debut. Flick gains a valuable tactical option from deep Barcelona dominated possession with 72% of the ball and completed 689 passes against Sabah, reinforcing their position among the Champions League’s leading passing teams. On that note, De Jong’s role was crucial as it offered Flick a solution that is certainly not limited to covering a defensive vacancy. Rather, his positioning allows Barcelona to build attacks through a player who understands midfield spaces, while his passing range helps dictate the tempo from the back. Simply put, the Dutchman is effectively operating as a deep-lying organiser, combining the responsibilities of a centre-back with the distribution qualities of a midfielder.

title: Alex Eala shares how it feels to be a part of a golden generation of sport in the Philippines, ‘we’re all excelling’
summary: Alexandra Eala’s season may be officially over, but she is far from enjoying the relaxation she has earned. After all, her schedule is perhaps the...
content: Alexandra Eala’s season may be officially over, but she is far from enjoying the relaxation she has earned. After all, her schedule is perhaps the most relentless on the WTA Tour, given what a national treasure she has become in such a short space of time in the Philippines. Having shot from seemingly relative obscurity to instant superstardom during the 2024 Miami Open, since then, this youngster has only continued to build on that stunning foundation. Now, she sits at a career-high ranking, having just enjoyed her best-ever run at two Grand Slam events, beaten countless top ten players, and won her first WTA Tour-level trophy too. However, with each new milestone comes added pressure, particularly given how important Alexandra Eala has already proven herself to sport in the Philippines. Speaking at her recent homecoming, she reiterated this point about pressure, whilst also heralding the new wave of talent propping up sport in her home country. Alexandra Eala explains what is difficult about achieving a career-high ranking this year Speaking to reporters during a press conference at the Pasig Central Elementary School earlier this week, Eala began with a word on her ranking. After all, the 21-year-old actually managed to sneak into 15th before the WTA season had officially concluded, a new career-high ranking. Discussing this new peak, Eala admitted there is a difficulty that comes with reaching such heights. She claimed: “Of course, it’s very difficult. The higher you go on the mountain, the steeper it gets. “So I’m definitely not expecting anything easy. Nothing fulfilling ever really comes easily. So I’ll do my best to stay there, and hopefully get even better.” Then, discussing sports in the Philippines in general, Eala added: “Of course, sports in general [is in a very good time], but I think women’s sports is having a moment right now. “So, to be part of a generation of such great athletes where we’re all excelling on the world stage, that’s an amazing thing, I believe, for the youth. “And it’s a testament to, it doesn’t matter where you come from or it doesn’t matter how you get there, it’s just that you’re able to get there.” Eala also had a message for her fans ahead of her exhibition match in the Philippines , which will take place just next month. She is also up for a WTA award that has previously been won by Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova .

title: Australian Open chief officially confirms Jannik Sinner will miss 2027 event after speaking to his team
summary: Jannik Sinner has officially been confirmed to miss the 2027 Australian Open. Tennis fans were already expecting the Italian to miss out on the opening...
content: Jannik Sinner has officially been confirmed to miss the 2027 Australian Open. Tennis fans were already expecting the Italian to miss out on the opening Grand Slam of the season, with Sinner having undergone knee surgery earlier this week. But his impending absence has now been made official by Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo. Jannik Sinner confirmed to miss 2027 Australian Open AFP have received a statement from the Tennis Australia chief, which reads: “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the AO in January following his recent surgery. “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon.” It’s a big blow for the Australian Open to take place without one of the biggest stars of the game, with everyone from fans to his fellow players impacted. Many fans will be gutted not to see the five-time Grand Slam champion in Melbourne, particularly given that two of his titles have arrived there. However, perhaps many of his ATP rivals will be breathing a sigh of relief given that historical success. Alexander Zverev stepped up in his absence and the absence of Carlos Alcaraz throughout the 2026 Grand Slam season, and there is now an opportunity to do the same without Sinner at the Australian Open. What is Jannik Sinner’s Australian Open record? The Italian has made seven appearances at the hard-court major, from which he boasts two titles and a 27-5 win-loss record. He first lifted the prestigious trophy in 2024 after a final victory over Daniil Medvedev, and went on to defend his title in 2025 by beating Zverev. This season the former world number one reached the semifinals, where he was beaten by Novak Djokovic in a five-set thriller. His ATP rival Carlos Alcaraz then defeated the Serbian to claim the title and indeed complete the career Grand Slam. Sinner can follow in the footsteps of the Spaniard by winning the French Open, but it remains to be seen if he will be fit enough to take on the clay-court Grand Slam in Paris next year. For now, his rehabilitation following surgery will be well underway, with Alcaraz among the players wishing Sinner well after the procedure.

title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open after knee surgery
summary: The World No 2 has not played since defending his Wimbledon title
content: Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery . The World No 2 has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first grand slam tournament of 2027. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery. “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028.” The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee. Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: “Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. “After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. “I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.” The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse. Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place. Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner’s surgery. “The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He’s young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I’m sure he’s going to come back even stronger, even better,” Alcaraz said on Wednesday. Zverev added: “”We know that he’s mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months’ time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing.”

title: Bizarre Legal Situation Develops Over Bill Watts’ Mid-South Wrestling (WWE News)
summary: WWE looking to bring back Mid-South Wrestling?
content: WWE Earlier this week, WWE filed a trademark for "Mid-South Wrestling." Mid-South Wrestling was the promotion run by ' Cowboy' Bill Watts from 1979 to 1986, becoming one of the hottest territories in the business and housing so many of the major stars of the day and of the future, from the Junkyard Dog to Ted DiBiase, to Magnum T.A., to Jim Duggan, to 'Dr. Death' Steve Williams, to Jake Roberts, to a young Shawn Michaels, to the Midnight Express, to the Rock 'n' Roll Express, and many, many more. The promotion rebranded as the Universal Wrestling Federation - not to be confused with Herb Abrams' company of the same name - in '86, then closed its doors for good the following year. Per POST Wrestling , Tuesday saw WWE file a trademark for the "Mid-South Wrestling" name for purposes of "Entertainment services, namely, a show about professional wrestling," suggesting the market leader could be looking to relaunch Mid-South in some form or fashion. What makes this trademark application all the more interesting is that it comes mere days after PRODUCE and Razor Pro Wrestling announced plans to revive the Mid-South Wrestling brand, starting with an event in Fayetteville, Arkansas, on February 21st of next year. Orange Crush, the art project behind PRODUCE, has since taken to X to post a screenshot of what appears to be their separate "Mid-South Wrestling" trademark application from Monday, one day before WWE's filing. pic.twitter.com/yWjIgB0KpA — ORANGE CRUSH (@orangecrushart) November 25, 2026 It remains to be seen how all of this plays out, though it is worth noting that WWE acquired the Mid-South library in 2012, purchasing that from Bill Watts' ex-wife, Ene, who herself acquired the library as part of her divorce from Cowboy.
